title.en: Volume 311 Biographies 70: Yan Shu, Pang Ji and Grandson: Gongsun, Wang Sui, Zhang Dexiang, Lu Yijian and Son: Gongchao, Gong Bi, Gong Ru, Zhang Shixun
title.raw: 卷三百十一 列傳第七十 晏殊 龐籍孫:恭孫 王隨 章得象 呂夷簡子:公綽 公弼 公孺 張士遜 Volume 311 Biographies 70: Yan Shu, Pang Ji and Grandson: Gongsun, Wang Sui, Zhang Dexiang, Lu Yijian and Son: Gongchao, Gong Bi, Gong Ru, Zhang Shixun

sentences.zh: 晏殊，字同叔，撫州臨川人。

translations.literal: Yan Shu, styled Tongshu, was a man of Linchuan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shu, styled Tongshu, was a native of Linchuan in Fuzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七歲能屬文，景德初，張知白安撫江南，以神童薦之。

translations.literal: At age seven he could compose literary pieces. At the beginning of the Jingde era, Zhang Zhibai, as pacification commissioner of Jiangnan, recommended him as a divine youth.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could already compose literary pieces. Early in the Jingde era, when Zhang Zhibai was pacifying Jiangnan, he recommended Shu as a child prodigy.

sentences.zh: 帝召殊與進士千餘人並試廷中，殊神氣不懾，援筆立成。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Shu together with more than a thousand jinshi to be examined together in the palace hall. Shu's spirit showed no fear; he took up his brush and completed the composition at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Shu to take the palace examination alongside more than a thousand jinshi candidates. Shu showed no sign of fear; he took up his brush and finished at once.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉賞，賜同進士出身。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and rewarded him, granting him the status of tong jinshi chushen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and rewarded him, granting him the rank of tong jinshi chushen.

sentences.zh: 宰相寇準曰：「殊江外人。」

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Kou Zhun said: "Shu is a man from beyond the Yangtze."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Kou Zhun said, "Shu is a man from south of the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 帝顧曰：「張九齡非江外人邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor turned and said: "Was Zhang Jiuling not also a man from beyond the Yangtze?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor turned and said, "Was Zhang Jiuling not also from south of the Yangtze?"

sentences.zh: 後二日，覆試詩、賦、論，殊奏：「臣嘗私習此賦，請試他題。」

translations.literal: Two days later, when he was re-examined in poetry, fu, and discourse, Shu submitted: "Your subject has privately studied this fu composition; I request that another topic be assigned."
translations.idiomatic: Two days later, when he was re-examined in poetry, fu, and discourse, Shu submitted, "I have already studied this fu topic on my own; please assign another."

sentences.zh: 帝愛其不欺，既成，數稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired his honesty. When the composition was finished, he repeatedly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired his honesty. When the new composition was done, he praised it again and again.

sentences.zh: 擢秘書省正字，秘閣讀書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Rectifier of Texts in the Secretariat and assigned to read in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Rectifier of Texts in the Secretariat and assigned to study in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 命直史館陳彭年察其所與游處者，每稱許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Chen Pengnian of the Historiography Office to investigate those with whom Shu associated; each time he reported praise.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Chen Pengnian of the Historiography Office to look into those with whom Shu kept company; each time Pengnian reported favorably on him.

sentences.zh: 明年，召試中書，遷太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: The following year he was summoned for examination at the Secretariat and promoted to Ceremonial Attendant in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned for examination at the Secretariat and promoted to Ceremonial Attendant in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 東封恩，遷光祿寺丞，為集賢校理。

translations.literal: During the eastern feng enfeoffment rewards, he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: During the rewards granted for the eastern feng rites, he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 喪父，歸臨川，奪服起之，從祀太清宮。

translations.literal: When his father died, he returned to Linchuan; his mourning was cut short and he was recalled to accompany the sacrifice at the Temple of the Grand Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he returned to Linchuan; his mourning was cut short and he was recalled to take part in the sacrifice at the Temple of the Grand Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 詔修寶訓，同判太常禮院。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compile the Precious Instructions and to serve concurrently as vice-director of the Ritual Court in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compile the Precious Instructions and concurrently to serve as vice-director of the Ritual Court in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 喪母，求終服，不許。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he requested to complete the full mourning period but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he asked to observe the full mourning period, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常寺丞，擢左正言、直史館，為昇王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, elevated to Left Remonstrator and compiler in the Historiography Office, and appointed recorder for the Heir Apparent's Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, elevated to Left Remonstrator and compiler in the Historiography Office, and appointed recorder in the Heir Apparent's Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 歲中，遷尚書戶部員外郎，為太子舍人，尋知制誥，判集賢院。

translations.literal: Within the year he was promoted to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue in the Secretariat, became Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and soon was made drafter of edicts and put in charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was promoted to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue, became Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and soon was made drafter of edicts and put in charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 久之，為翰林學士，遷左庶子。

translations.literal: After some time he became a Hanlin Academician and was promoted to Left Subordinate at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became a Hanlin Academician and was promoted to Left Subordinate of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝每訪殊以事，率用方寸小紙細書，已答奏，輒並稿封上，帝重其慎密。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor consulted Shu on affairs, Shu invariably wrote his answers in fine script on a small square of paper; once he had submitted his reply, he would seal up the draft together with it—the Emperor valued his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor consulted Shu on affairs, Shu invariably wrote his answers in fine script on a small square of paper; once he had submitted his reply, he would seal up the draft and send it up with the memorial—the Emperor greatly valued his discretion.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，章獻明肅太后奉遺詔權聽政。

translations.literal: When Renzong succeeded to the throne, Empress Dowager Zhangxian Mingsu, acting on the late emperor's testament, held regency.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, Empress Dowager Zhangxian Mingsu, acting on the late emperor's testament, held regency.

sentences.zh: 宰相丁謂、樞密使曹利用，各欲獨見奏事，無敢決其議者，殊建言：「群臣奏事太后者，垂簾聽之，皆毋得見。」

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Ding Wei and Military Affairs Commissioner Cao Liyong each wished to be received alone to present memorials; no one dared settle their dispute. Shu proposed: "When the officials present memorials to the Empress Dowager, she shall listen from behind the curtain; none shall be granted audience."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Ding Wei and Military Affairs Commissioner Cao Liyong each wanted to be received alone to present memorials, and no one dared settle their dispute. Shu proposed, "When officials present memorials to the Empress Dowager, she should listen from behind the curtain; none of them should be granted an audience."

sentences.zh: 議遂定。

translations.literal: The policy was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: The policy was thereby settled.

sentences.zh: 遷右諫議大夫兼侍讀學士，太后謂東宮舊臣，恩不稱，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Remonstrating Grandee and concurrent Lecturing Academician. The Empress Dowager said that as a former Eastern Palace retainer his favor was not commensurate with his service, and he was given the additional title of Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrating Grandee and concurrent Lecturing Academician. The Empress Dowager said that as a former Eastern Palace retainer his rewards did not match his service, and he was given the additional title of Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 預修《真宗實錄》。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Zhenzong.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Zhenzong.

sentences.zh: 進禮部侍郎，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of Rites and appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Vice Minister of Rites and appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上疏論張耆不可為樞密使，忤太后旨。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial arguing that Zhang Qi should not be made Military Affairs Commissioner, thereby offending the Empress Dowager's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial arguing that Zhang Qi was unfit to be Military Affairs Commissioner, thereby offending the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 坐從幸玉清昭應宮從者持笏後至，殊怒，以笏撞之折齒，御史彈奏，罷知宣州。

translations.literal: While accompanying the Emperor on a visit to the Jade Clarity Zhaoying Palace, an attendant arrived late carrying a tablet. Shu in anger struck him with the tablet and broke his teeth. The censors impeached him, and he was dismissed to serve as prefect of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the Emperor on a visit to the Jade Clarity Zhaoying Palace, an attendant arrived late carrying a court tablet. Shu in anger struck him with the tablet and broke his teeth. The censors impeached him, and he was dismissed to serve as prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 數月，改應天府，延范仲淹以教生徒。

translations.literal: After several months he was transferred to Yingtian Prefecture, where he invited Fan Zhongyan to instruct the students.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was transferred to Yingtian Prefecture, where he invited Fan Zhongyan to teach the students.

sentences.zh: 自五代以來，天下學校廢，興學自殊始。

translations.literal: Since the Five Dynasties, schools throughout the realm had fallen into disuse; the revival of learning began with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties, schools throughout the empire had fallen into disuse; the revival of learning began with Shu.

sentences.zh: 召拜御史中丞，改資政殿學士、兼翰林侍讀學士，兵部侍郎、兼秘書監，為三司使，復為樞密副使，未拜，改參知政事，加尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief, then made Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and concurrent Hanlin Lecturing Academician, Vice Minister of War and concurrent Director of the Palace Library, Commissioner of the Three Departments, and again Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs; before he could take the latter post he was made Participant in Governance and given the additional title of Left Vice Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief, then made Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and concurrent Hanlin Lecturing Academician, Vice Minister of War and concurrent Director of the Palace Library, Commissioner of the Three Departments, and again Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs; before he could take the latter post he was made Participant in Governance and given the additional title of Left Vice Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太后謁太廟，有請服袞冕者，太后以問，殊以《周官》后服對。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple, some proposed that she wear the gun and mian robes. The Empress Dowager asked Shu, and he answered with reference to the queen's attire in the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple, some proposed that she wear the gun and mian robes. The Empress Dowager asked Shu, and he answered by citing the queen's attire described in the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，以禮部尚書罷知亳州，徙陳州，遷刑部尚書，以本官兼御史中丞，復為三司使。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager died, he was dismissed from office as Minister of Rites and made prefect of Bozhou, then transferred to Chenzhou, promoted to Minister of Justice, and with his existing rank made concurrent Censor-in-Chief and again Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager died, he left office as Minister of Rites and was made prefect of Bozhou, then transferred to Chenzhou, promoted to Minister of Justice, and with his existing rank made concurrent Censor-in-Chief and again Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 陝西方用兵，殊請罷內臣監兵，不以陣圖授諸將，使得應敵為攻守；

translations.literal: When war was waged in Shaanxi, Shu requested that eunuch supervisors of troops be abolished, that battle formations not be handed to the generals in advance, and that they be allowed to attack and defend as circumstances required;
translations.idiomatic: When war was being waged in Shaanxi, Shu requested that eunuch supervisors of troops be abolished, that battle formations not be handed to the generals in advance, and that they be allowed to attack and defend as circumstances required;

sentences.zh: 及募弓箭手教之，以備戰鬥。

translations.literal: and that bowmen be recruited and trained for battle.
translations.idiomatic: and that bowmen be recruited and trained for combat.

sentences.zh: 又請出宮中長物助邊費，凡他司之領財利者，悉罷還度支。

translations.literal: He also requested that surplus goods from the palace be released to help pay frontier expenses, and that all other agencies managing revenues be abolished and returned to the Department of State Finance.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that surplus goods from the palace be released to help pay frontier expenses, and that all other agencies managing revenues be abolished and their functions returned to the Department of State Finance.

sentences.zh: 悉為施行。

translations.literal: All were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 康定初，知樞密院事，遂為樞密使。

translations.literal: Early in the Kangding era he was made Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and then Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangding era he was made Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and then Military Affairs Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Tong Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Grand Councilor of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 慶歷中，拜集賢殿學士、同平章事，兼樞密使。

translations.literal: During the Qingli era he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Tong Pingzhangshi, and concurrent Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Grand Councilor, and concurrent Military Affairs Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 殊平居好賢，當世知名之士，如范仲淹、孔道輔皆出其門。

translations.literal: In ordinary life Shu delighted in worthy men; renowned figures of the age, such as Fan Zhongyan and Kong Daofu, all came from his circle.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary life Shu delighted in worthy men; renowned figures of the age, such as Fan Zhongyan and Kong Daofu, had all passed through his circle.

sentences.zh: 及為相，益務進賢材，而仲淹與韓琦、富弼皆進用，至於臺閣，多一時之賢。

translations.literal: When he became chief councilor, he strove all the more to advance worthy talent; Fan Zhongyan, Han Qi, and Fu Bi were all promoted, and in the central offices there were many men of talent for that age.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became chief councilor, he strove all the more to advance worthy talent; Fan Zhongyan, Han Qi, and Fu Bi were all promoted, and the central offices came to hold many of the finest men of the age.

sentences.zh: 帝亦奮然有意，欲因群材以更治，而小人權幸皆不便。

translations.literal: The Emperor too was stirred with purpose and wished to use this gathering of talent to reform governance, but petty men in positions of favor all found it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor too was stirred with purpose and wished to use this gathering of talent to reform governance, but petty men in positions of favor all found it inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 殊出歐陽修為河北都轉運，諫官奏留，不許。

translations.literal: Shu sent Ouyang Xiu out as Director-General Transport Commissioner for Hebei; remonstrating officials memorialized to keep him, but permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Shu sent Ouyang Xiu out as Director-General Transport Commissioner for Hebei; remonstrating officials memorialized to keep him at court, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 孫甫、蔡襄上言：「宸妃生聖躬為天下主，而殊嘗被詔志宸妃墓，沒而不言。」

translations.literal: Sun Fu and Cai Xiang submitted: "The Noble Consort bore the sacred person who became ruler of all under Heaven, yet Shu was once ordered to compose the epitaph for her tomb and, after her death, said nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu and Cai Xiang submitted, "The Noble Consort bore the sacred person who became ruler of all under Heaven, yet Shu was once ordered to compose the epitaph for her tomb and, after her death, said nothing about it."

sentences.zh: 又奏論殊役官兵治僦舍以規利。

translations.literal: They also memorialized that Shu had used government troops to manage rented lodgings for profit.
translations.idiomatic: They also memorialized that Shu had used government troops to manage rented lodgings for profit.

sentences.zh: 坐是，降工部尚書、知穎州。

translations.literal: For this he was demoted to Minister of Works and made prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was demoted to Minister of Works and made prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 然殊以章獻太后方臨朝，故志不敢斥言；

translations.literal: Yet because Empress Dowager Zhangxian was still regent, Shu had not dared speak plainly in the epitaph;
translations.idiomatic: Yet because Empress Dowager Zhangxian was still regent, Shu had not dared speak plainly in the epitaph;

sentences.zh: 而所役兵，乃輔臣例宣借者，時以謂非殊罪。

translations.literal: and the troops he had used were the sort that chief ministers routinely borrowed by imperial order—at the time many held that this was not Shu's fault.
translations.idiomatic: and the troops he had used were the sort that chief ministers routinely borrowed by imperial order—at the time many held that this was not Shu's fault.

sentences.zh: 殊性剛簡，奉養清儉。

translations.literal: Shu's nature was stern and spare; in supporting his household he was pure and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's nature was stern and spare; in supporting his household he lived plainly and frugally.

sentences.zh: 累典州，吏民頗畏其悁急。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly governed prefectures, officials and commoners alike feared his narrow urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Having repeatedly governed prefectures, officials and commoners alike feared his stern impatience.

sentences.zh: 善知人，富弼、楊察，皆其婿也。

translations.literal: He was skilled at knowing men; Fu Bi and Yang Cha were both his sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at judging men; Fu Bi and Yang Cha were both his sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 殊為宰相兼樞密使，而弼為副使，辭所兼，詔不許，其信遇如此。

translations.literal: Shu served as chief councilor and concurrent Military Affairs Commissioner while Bi was vice commissioner; Bi declined the concurrent post, but an edict did not permit it—such was the trust shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu served as chief councilor and concurrent Military Affairs Commissioner while Bi was vice commissioner; Bi declined the concurrent post, but an edict would not allow it—such was the trust the court placed in him.

sentences.zh: 文章贍麗，應用不窮，尤工詩，閒雅有情思，晚歲篤學不倦。

translations.literal: His literary compositions were rich and beautiful, inexhaustible in practical use; he was especially skilled in poetry, refined and elegant with feeling and thought, and in his later years he studied devotedly without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: His literary compositions were rich and beautiful and inexhaustible in practical use; he was especially skilled in poetry, refined and elegant with feeling and thought, and in his later years he studied devotedly without tiring.

sentences.zh: 文集二百四十卷，及刪次梁、陳以後名臣述作，為《集選》一百卷。

translations.literal: His collected writings ran to 240 juan, and he also selected and arranged the compositions of famous ministers from the Liang and Chen onward into the Collected Selections in 100 juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to 240 juan, and he also selected and arranged the compositions of famous ministers from the Liang and Chen onward into the Collected Selections in 100 juan.

sentences.zh: 子知止，為朝請大夫。

translations.literal: His son Zhizhi served as Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhizhi served as Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences.

sentences.zh: 龐籍，字醇之，單州成武人。

translations.literal: Pang Ji, styled Chunzhi, was a man of Chengwu in Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji, styled Chunzhi, was a native of Chengwu in Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，為黃州司理參軍，知州夏竦以為有宰相器。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as judicial assistant in Huangzhou; Prefect Xia Song regarded him as having the makings of a chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as judicial assistant in Huangzhou; Prefect Xia Song regarded him as having the makings of a chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 調開封府兵曹參軍，知府薛奎薦為法曹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military assistant in the Kaifeng Prefecture government; Prefect Xue Kui recommended him for the legal bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military assistant in the Kaifeng Prefecture government; Prefect Xue Kui recommended him for the legal bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺丞、知襄邑縣。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and made magistrate of Xiangyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and made magistrate of Xiangyi County.

sentences.zh: 預修《天聖編敕》，為刑部詳覆官。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Tiansheng Compiled Statutes and served as reviewing officer in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Tiansheng Compiled Statutes and served as reviewing officer in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 擢群牧判官，因轉封言：「舊制不以國馬假臣下，重武備也。

translations.literal: He was promoted to judge in the Pasturage Commission and, on a memorial in transit, said: "By old regulation state horses were not lent to officials below the throne, in order to emphasize military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judge in the Pasturage Commission and, on a memorial in transit, said, "By old regulation state horses were not lent to officials below the throne, in order to emphasize military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 樞密院以帶甲馬借內侍楊懷敏，群牧覆奏，乃賜一馬，三日，乃復借之，數日而復罷。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs lent an armored horse to the eunuch Yang Huaimin; the Pasturage Commission reviewed and reported back, and only then was one horse granted. Three days later it was lent again, and after several days the loan was revoked again.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs lent an armored horse to the eunuch Yang Huaimin; the Pasturage Commission reviewed and reported back, and only then was one horse granted. Three days later it was lent again, and after several days the loan was revoked again.

sentences.zh: 樞密掌機命，反覆乃如此。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs holds command of critical affairs, yet it vacillated in this way.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs holds command of critical affairs, yet it vacillated in this way.

sentences.zh: 平時，百官奏事上前，不自批章，止送中書、樞密院。

translations.literal: In ordinary times, when the hundred officials presented memorials before the throne, the Emperor did not himself endorse the documents but sent them only to the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times, when officials presented memorials before the throne, the Emperor did not himself endorse the documents but sent them only to the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 近歲璽書內降，寖多於舊，無以防偏請、杜幸門矣。

translations.literal: In recent years sealed edicts issued from within the palace have gradually become more numerous than before, so that there is no way to guard against partial requests or shut the gate to favor-seeking.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years sealed edicts issued from within the palace have gradually become more numerous than before, so that there is no way to guard against partial requests or shut the gate to favor-seeking.

sentences.zh: 往者，王世融以公主子毆府吏，法當贖金，特停任。

translations.literal: Formerly, Wang Shirong, as son of a princess, beat a prefectural official; by law he should have paid a redemption fine, but he was specially suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, Wang Shirong, as son of a princess, beat a prefectural official; by law he should have paid a redemption fine, but he was specially suspended from office.

sentences.zh: 近作坊料物庫主吏盜官物，輒自逃避。

translations.literal: Recently the chief clerk of the workshop materials storehouse stole government goods and then fled of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the chief clerk of the workshop materials storehouse stole government goods and then fled of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 以宮掖之親，三司遽罷追究。

translations.literal: Because of kinship with the palace, the Three Departments abruptly halted the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Because of kinship with the palace, the Three Departments abruptly halted the investigation.

sentences.zh: 今日聖斷乃異於昔，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Today's sacred decision differs from the past; your subject is privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Today's sacred decision differs from the past; your subject is privately perplexed.

sentences.zh: 祥符令檢下稍嚴，胥吏相率空縣而去，令坐罷免。

translations.literal: In Xiangfu the magistrate's inspections below were somewhat strict; clerks left the county in a body, and the magistrate was dismissed from office for it.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiangfu the magistrate's inspections below were somewhat strict; clerks left the county in a body, and the magistrate was dismissed from office for it.

sentences.zh: 若是，則清強者沮矣。」

translations.literal: If this is so, then the upright and forceful will be discouraged."
translations.idiomatic: If this is so, then the upright and forceful will be discouraged."

sentences.zh: 久之，出知秀州，召為殿中侍御史，章獻太后遺誥章惠太后議軍國事；

translations.literal: After some time he was sent out as prefect of Xiuzhou, then summoned as Palace Attendant Censor. Empress Dowager Zhangxian's testament directed Empress Dowager Zhanghui to deliberate on state and military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out as prefect of Xiuzhou, then summoned as Palace Attendant Censor. Empress Dowager Zhangxian's testament directed Empress Dowager Zhanghui to deliberate on state and military affairs;

sentences.zh: 籍請下閣門，取垂簾儀制盡燔之。

translations.literal: Ji requested that the Gate Office be ordered to take out the regulations for listening from behind the curtain and burn them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ji requested that the Gate Office be ordered to take out the regulations for listening from behind the curtain and burn them all.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「陛下躬親萬機，用人宜辨邪正、防朋黨，擢進近列，願採公論，毋令出於執政。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Your Majesty personally attends to the myriad affairs of state; in appointing men you should distinguish the upright from the depraved and guard against faction, and in promoting those near at hand you should wish to take public opinion—let it not come from the chief ministers alone."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "Your Majesty personally attends to the myriad affairs of state; in appointing men you should distinguish the upright from the depraved and guard against faction, and in promoting those near at hand you should rely on public opinion—let appointments not come from the chief ministers alone."

sentences.zh: 孔道輔謂人曰：「言事官多觀望宰相意，獨龐醇之，天子御史也。」

translations.literal: Kong Daofu said to others: "Most remonstrating officials watch the chief councilor's intent; only Pang Chunzhi is the Son of Heaven's censor."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Daofu said to others, "Most remonstrating officials watch the chief councilor's intent; only Pang Chunzhi is the Son of Heaven's censor."

sentences.zh: 為開封府判官，尚美人遣內侍稱教旨免工人市租。

translations.literal: As judge in the Kaifeng Prefecture government, the Lady Shang sent a eunuch claiming an edict to exempt workers from market rents.
translations.idiomatic: As judge in the Kaifeng Prefecture government, the Lady Shang sent a eunuch claiming an edict to exempt workers from market rents.

sentences.zh: 籍言：「祖宗以來，未有美人稱教旨下府者，當杖內侍。」

translations.literal: Ji said: "Since the founding ancestors, no palace lady has ever sent an edict down to a prefectural office; the eunuch should be beaten with the staff."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Since the founding ancestors, no palace lady has ever sent an edict down to a prefectural office; the eunuch should be beaten with the staff."

sentences.zh: 詔有司：「自今宮中傳命，毋得輒受。」

translations.literal: An edict was issued to the responsible offices: "From now on, orders transmitted from within the palace must not be accepted at will."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to the responsible offices, "From now on, orders transmitted from within the palace must not be accepted at will."

sentences.zh: 數劾范諷罪，諷善李迪，皆寢不報，反坐言宮禁事不得實，以祠部員外郎罷為廣南東路轉運使。

translations.literal: He repeatedly impeached Fan Feng for offenses; Feng was friendly with Li Di, and all were shelved without response. Instead Ji was punished for speaking on palace matters without substantiation, dismissed as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and made Transport Commissioner for the Eastern Circuit of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly impeached Fan Feng for offenses; Feng was friendly with Li Di, and all were shelved without response. Instead Ji was punished for speaking on palace matters without substantiation, dismissed as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and made Transport Commissioner for the Eastern Circuit of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 又言范諷事有不盡如奏，諷坐貶，籍亦降太常博士、知臨江軍。

translations.literal: He again spoke on Fan Feng's case, saying it had not been fully as memorialized; Feng was demoted for it, and Ji was also reduced to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made military prefect of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He again spoke on Fan Feng's case, saying it had not been fully as memorialized; Feng was demoted for it, and Ji was also reduced to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made military prefect of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 尋復官，徙福建轉運使。

translations.literal: Soon his office was restored, and he was transferred as Transport Commissioner for Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his office was restored, and he was transferred as Transport Commissioner for Fujian.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年，為侍御史，改刑部員外郎、知雜事，判大理寺，進天章閣待制。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou he became Attending Censor, then was made Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice with charge of miscellaneous affairs and concurrent judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and advanced to Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingyou he became Attending Censor, then was made Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice with charge of miscellaneous affairs and concurrent judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and advanced to Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，為陝西體量安撫使。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he was made Investigating and Pacification Commissioner for Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he was made Investigating and Pacification Commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 坐令開封府吏馮士元市女口，降知汝州。

translations.literal: Because he had ordered the Kaifeng official Feng Shiyuan to purchase female dependents, he was demoted to prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had ordered the Kaifeng official Feng Shiyuan to purchase female dependents, he was demoted to prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 徒同州，就除陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Tongzhou and then appointed on the spot as Director-General Transport Commissioner for Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Tongzhou and then appointed on the spot as Director-General Transport Commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 文彥博鞫黃德和獄，未上，詔籍同案。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo was investigating the case of Huang Dehe but had not yet submitted it; an edict ordered Ji to join the case.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo was investigating the case of Huang Dehe but had not yet submitted it; an edict ordered Ji to join the case.

sentences.zh: 籍言曰：「德和退怯當誅。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Dehe retreated in cowardice and should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Dehe retreated in cowardice and should be executed.

sentences.zh: 劉平力戰而沒，宜加恤其子孫。」

translations.literal: Liu Ping fought fiercely and perished; his sons and grandsons should receive added consolation."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping fought fiercely and perished; his sons and grandsons should receive added consolation."

sentences.zh: 又建言：「頻歲災異，天久不雨。

translations.literal: He also proposed: "In successive years there have been disasters and anomalies, and Heaven has long withheld rain.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed, "In successive years there have been disasters and anomalies, and Heaven has long withheld rain.

sentences.zh: 宮中費用奢靡，出納不嚴，須索煩多，有司無從鉤校虛實。

translations.literal: Expenditure within the palace is extravagant; receipts and disbursements are not strict, requisitions are numerous and troublesome, and the responsible offices have no way to verify what is real or false.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditure within the palace is extravagant; receipts and disbursements are not strict, requisitions are numerous and troublesome, and the responsible offices have no way to verify what is real or false.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂凡乘輿所費，宮中所用，宜務加裁抑，取則先帝，修德弭災之道也。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say that all expenses of the imperial carriage and all uses within the palace should be vigorously curtailed, taking the former emperor as the standard—this is the way to cultivate virtue and quell disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures to say that all expenses of the imperial carriage and all uses within the palace should be vigorously curtailed, taking the former emperor as the standard—this is the way to cultivate virtue and quell disasters.

sentences.zh: 今宿兵西鄙，將士力戰，弗獲功賞；

translations.literal: Now troops are stationed on the western frontier; officers and soldiers fight with all their strength yet do not receive rewards for merit;
translations.idiomatic: Now troops are stationed on the western frontier; officers and soldiers fight with all their strength yet do not receive rewards for merit;

sentences.zh: 而內官、醫官、樂官，無功勞，享豐賜，天下指目，謂之『三官』。

translations.literal: while inner attendants, medical officers, and music officers, without merit or labor, enjoy rich largesse—the realm points at them and calls them the 'Three Offices.'
translations.idiomatic: while inner attendants, medical officers, and music officers, without merit or labor, enjoy rich largesse—the realm points at them and calls them the 'Three Offices.'

sentences.zh: 願少裁損，無厚賚予，專勵戰功，寇不足平也。」

translations.literal: I wish that they be somewhat reduced, that lavish gifts not be given, and that merit in battle alone be encouraged—then the enemy will not be hard to subdue."
translations.idiomatic: I wish that they be somewhat reduced, that lavish gifts not be given, and that merit in battle alone be encouraged—then the enemy will not be hard to subdue."

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣直學士、知延州，俄兼鄜延都總管、經略安撫緣邊招討使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Yanzhou; soon he was also made Director-General of the Yan and Yan Circuits, Pacification Commissioner, and Frontier Recruiting Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Yanzhou; soon he was also made Director-General of the Yan and Yan Circuits, Pacification Commissioner, and Frontier Recruiting Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，改延州觀察使，力辭，換左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The following year he was made Observation Commissioner of Yanzhou; he strenuously declined, and was transferred to Left Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Observation Commissioner of Yanzhou; he strenuously declined, and was transferred to Left Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 自元昊陷金明、承平、塞門、安遠、栲栳砦，破五龍川，邊民焚掠殆盡，籍至，稍葺治之。

translations.literal: Since Yuan Hao had taken Jinming, Chengping, Saimen, Anyuan, and Kaolao Stockade and broken through Wulongchuan, frontier commoners had been burned and plundered almost to extinction; when Ji arrived, he gradually repaired the damage.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuan Hao had taken Jinming, Chengping, Saimen, Anyuan, and Kaolao Stockade and broken through Wulongchuan, frontier commoners had been burned and plundered almost to extinction; when Ji arrived, he gradually repaired the damage.

sentences.zh: 戍兵十萬無壁壘，皆散處城中，畏籍，莫敢犯法。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand garrison troops had no fortifications and were all scattered within the city; they feared Ji and none dared break the law.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand garrison troops had no fortifications and were all scattered within the city; they feared Ji and none dared break the law.

sentences.zh: 金明西北有渾州川，土沃衍。

translations.literal: Northwest of Jinming was Hunzhou Stream, with rich and expansive soil.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Jinming was Hunzhou Stream, with rich and expansive soil.

sentences.zh: 川尾曰橋子谷，寇出入之隘道。

translations.literal: At the stream's end was Qiaozi Valley, a narrow passage by which the enemy came and went.
translations.idiomatic: At the stream's end was Qiaozi Valley, a narrow passage by which the enemy came and went.

sentences.zh: 使部將狄青將萬餘人，築招安砦於谷旁，數募民耕種，收粟以贍軍。

translations.literal: He had his subordinate general Di Qing lead more than ten thousand men, build Zhao'an Stockade beside the valley, repeatedly recruit commoners to farm and plant, and collect grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched subordinate general Di Qing with more than ten thousand troops to build Zhao'an Stockade beside the valley, repeatedly recruited local farmers to cultivate the land, and used the harvest to provision the army.

sentences.zh: 周美襲取承平砦，王信築龍安砦，悉復所亡地，築十一城。

translations.literal: Zhou Mei raided and took Chengping Stockade; Wang Xin built Long'an Stockade; they fully recovered all lost territory and built eleven cities.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mei seized Chengping Stockade by surprise, Wang Xin erected Long'an Stockade, and together they fully restored the lost territory and constructed eleven fortified towns.

sentences.zh: 及開癿名、平戎道，通永和、烏仁關，更東西陣法為方陣，頗損益兵械。

translations.literal: Moreover he opened the Qingjian route and the Pingrong Road, linked Yonghe and Wuren Pass, changed the east-west battle formation to the square formation, and made many improvements and reductions to arms and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened the Qingjian route and the Pingrong Road, connected Yonghe and Wuren Pass, replaced the east-west formation tactics with square formations, and substantially revised the army's weapons and equipment.

sentences.zh: 元昊遣李文貴齎野利旺榮書來送款，籍曰：「此詐也。」

translations.literal: Yuan Hao sent Li Wengui bearing a letter from Yeli Wangrong to offer submission; Ji said: "This is deceit."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao sent Li Wengui with a letter from Yeli Wangrong offering peace terms; Ji said, "This is a ruse."

sentences.zh: 乃屯兵青澗城。

translations.literal: He then stationed troops at Qingjian City.
translations.idiomatic: With that he concentrated troops at Qingjian City.

sentences.zh: 後數月，果大寇定川，籍召文貴開諭之，遣去。

translations.literal: Several months later, a large raid on Dingchuan indeed occurred; Ji summoned Wengui, spoke frankly to admonish him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later the Tangut forces launched a major attack on Dingchuan as expected; Ji summoned Wengui, confronted him plainly, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 既而元昊又以旺榮書來，會帝厭兵，因招懷之，遣籍報書，使呼旺榮為太尉。

translations.literal: Before long Yuan Hao again sent a letter through Wangrong; as it happened the emperor had grown weary of war, and so sought to win them over; he had Ji reply with a letter addressing Wangrong as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuan Hao sent another letter via Wangrong; the emperor, weary of war, sought to conciliate the enemy and had Ji send a reply addressing Wangrong as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 籍曰：「太尉三公，非陪臣所得稱，使旺榮當之，則元昊不得臣矣。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Grand Commandant is one of the Three Dukes; it is not a title a vassal minister may bear. If Wangrong were to hold it, then Yuan Hao could no longer be a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Grand Commandant is one of the Three Dukes—not a title a tributary minister may claim. If Wangrong held it, Yuan Hao could no longer submit as a subject.

sentences.zh: 今其書自稱『寧令』或『謨寧令』，皆其官名也，於義無嫌。」

translations.literal: Now in their letter he styles himself 'Ningling' or 'Moningling'—both are his official titles—and in principle there is no objection."
translations.idiomatic: In their letter he calls himself 'Ningling' or 'Moningling'—both official titles of his—and that raises no objection in principle."

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 會敵新破涇原城砦，方議修復。

translations.literal: It happened that the enemy had newly destroyed the fortified towns of Jingyuan Circuit, and plans for repair were just underway.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the enemy had just overrun the fortified towns of Jingyuan Circuit, and the court was debating how to rebuild them.

sentences.zh: 使者往返，逾年，又遣賀從勖來，改名曰曩霄，稱男不稱臣。

translations.literal: Envoys shuttled back and forth for more than a year; then He Congxu was again sent, Yuan Hao changed his name to Nangxiao, and styled himself 'son' rather than 'subject.'
translations.idiomatic: After envoys traveled back and forth for over a year, He Congxu was dispatched again; Yuan Hao took the name Nangxiao and called himself 'son' instead of 'subject.'

sentences.zh: 籍不敢聞，從勖曰：「子事父，猶臣事君也。

translations.literal: Ji did not dare report this; Congxu said: "A son serving his father is like a subject serving his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Ji hesitated to relay this to the throne; Congxu said, "A son serving his father is no different from a subject serving his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 若得至京師，天子不許，更歸議之。」

translations.literal: If we can reach the capital and the Son of Heaven does not approve, we can return and discuss it again."
translations.idiomatic: If we reach the capital and the emperor withholds approval, we can return and negotiate further."

sentences.zh: 籍送使者闕下，因陳便宜，言：「羌久不通和市，國人愁怨。

translations.literal: Ji escorted the envoy to the imperial court and, taking the occasion to submit practical advice, said: "The Tangut people have long been cut off from border markets, and the populace is aggrieved and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Ji escorted the envoy to the capital and submitted a memorial on practical measures, saying, "The Tangut people have long lacked border trade, and their populace is growing restless.

sentences.zh: 今辭理寖順，必有改事中國之心，請遣使者申諭之。」

translations.literal: Now their language is gradually becoming compliant; they must harbor a mind to change their conduct toward China. I ask that an envoy be sent to explain and instruct them."
translations.idiomatic: Their rhetoric is growing more compliant, and they likely wish to change their stance toward the Middle Kingdom. I request that an envoy be sent to clarify our position."

sentences.zh: 朝廷採用其策。

translations.literal: The court adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 元昊既臣，召籍為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Once Yuan Hao had submitted as a subject, Ji was summoned to serve as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao submitted, Ji was recalled to the capital as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 籍言：「自陝西用兵，公私俱困，請並省官屬，退近塞之兵就食內地。」

translations.literal: Ji said: "Since the campaign in Shaanxi, both public and private resources have been exhausted. I ask that offices be consolidated and troops stationed near the frontier be withdrawn to draw provisions from the interior."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Since the western campaigns began, both state and private resources have been drained. I ask that offices be consolidated and frontier garrisons be brought inland to draw their provisions from the interior."

sentences.zh: 從之，於是頗省邊費。

translations.literal: The request was granted, and frontier expenses were substantially reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and frontier expenditures were substantially cut.

sentences.zh: 改參知政事，拜工部侍郎、樞密使，遷戶部，拜同中書門下平章事、昭文館大學士、監修國史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Grand Councilor, appointed Vice Minister of Works and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and appointed Chief Councilor through the Zhongshu and Menxia offices, Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and overseer of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Grand Councilor, appointed Vice Minister of Works and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and elevated to Chief Councilor, Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and overseer of the national history.

sentences.zh: 籍初入相，且獨員，而遽為昭文館大學士，出殊拜也。

translations.literal: When Ji first entered the council he was the sole appointee, yet was immediately made Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall—an exceptional promotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji first became chief councilor he was the only appointee, yet was immediately made Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall—an extraordinary elevation.

sentences.zh: 儂智高反，師數不利，遣狄青為宣撫使。

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao rebelled; the army suffered repeated setbacks, and Di Qing was dispatched as Military Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao rebelled and the army met repeated defeats, Di Qing was sent as Military Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 諫官韓絳謂武人不宜專任，帝以問籍。

translations.literal: Remonstrating official Han Jiang said a military man should not hold sole authority; the emperor asked Ji's view.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating official Han Jiang argued that a military man should not hold sole command; the emperor asked Ji for his opinion.

sentences.zh: 籍曰：「青起行伍，若以文臣副之，則號令不專，不如不遣。」

translations.literal: Ji said: "Qing rose from the ranks; if civil officials were paired with him, orders would not be unified—it would be better not to send him at all."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Qing rose from the ranks. If civil officials were placed alongside him, command would be divided—it would be better not to send him at all."

sentences.zh: 詔嶺南諸軍，皆受青節度。

translations.literal: An edict placed all armies of the Lingnan region under Qing's command.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed all southern armies under Qing's command.

sentences.zh: 既而捷書至，帝喜曰：「青破賊，卿之力也。」

translations.literal: Before long victory reports arrived; the emperor said with delight: "Qing's defeat of the rebels is your doing."
translations.idiomatic: When victory reports arrived, the emperor said joyfully, "Qing's defeat of the rebels is your achievement."

sentences.zh: 遂欲以青為樞密使、同平章事，籍力爭之，不聽。

translations.literal: He then wished to make Qing Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Chief Councilor; Ji strenuously opposed this, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then wanted to appoint Qing Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Chief Councilor; Ji fought the appointment strenuously, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 嶺南平，二廣舉人推恩者六百九十一人，論者以為過。

translations.literal: When the Lingnan region was pacified, six hundred ninety-one examination candidates from the two Guang circuits received preferential treatment; critics deemed this excessive.
translations.idiomatic: After the south was pacified, six hundred ninety-one examination candidates from the two Guang circuits received preferential treatment; critics considered this excessive.

sentences.zh: 頃之，齊州學究皇甫淵以捕賊功，法當賞錢，數上書求用。

translations.literal: Before long, Qi Prefecture classicist Huangfu Yuan, entitled by law to a cash reward for capturing bandits, repeatedly submitted memorials seeking appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, Qi Prefecture scholar Huangfu Yuan, entitled by law to a cash reward for capturing bandits, repeatedly petitioned for office.

sentences.zh: 道士趙清貺與籍姊家親，紿為淵白籍，乃與堂吏共受淵賂。

translations.literal: Daoist Zhao Qinggu was related by marriage to Ji's elder sister's family; he falsely claimed to speak on Yuan's behalf to Ji, and together with a clerk in Ji's office accepted bribes from Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist Zhao Qinggu was related by marriage to Ji's elder sister's family; he falsely claimed to speak for Yuan before Ji, and he and a clerk in Ji's office jointly accepted bribes from Yuan.

sentences.zh: 小吏訴之，下開封府，捕清貺，刺配遠州，道死。

translations.literal: A junior clerk reported this; the case went to Kaifeng Prefecture; Qinggu was arrested, tattooed and banished to a distant prefecture, and died en route.
translations.idiomatic: A junior clerk reported the matter to Kaifeng Prefecture; Qinggu was arrested, tattooed and banished to a distant prefecture, and died on the way.

sentences.zh: 韓絳言籍陰諷府杖殺清貺以滅口，覆之無狀。

translations.literal: Han Jiang said Ji had secretly prompted the prefecture to beat Qinggu to death to silence him; reinvestigation found no basis for this.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang charged that Ji had secretly urged the prefecture to beat Qinggu to death to silence him; a reinvestigation found no evidence.

sentences.zh: 言不已，乃罷知鄆州。

translations.literal: Han would not cease his accusations, and Ji was removed as prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Han would not let the matter drop, Ji was dismissed as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 居數月，加觀文殿大學士。

translations.literal: After several months he was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture.

sentences.zh: 拜昭德軍節度使、知永興軍，改幷州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhaode and prefect of Yongxing, then transferred to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Commissioner of Zhaode and prefect of Yongxing, then transferred to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗不豫，籍嘗密疏，請擇宗室之賢者為皇子，其言甚切。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong fell ill, Ji once sent a secret memorial asking that a worthy member of the imperial clan be selected as crown prince; his language was very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong fell ill, Ji sent a secret memorial urging that a worthy member of the imperial clan be chosen as crown prince; his words were urgent and forceful.

sentences.zh: 坐擅聽麟州築堡白草平，而州將武戡等為夏人所敗，復為觀文殿大學士、戶部侍郎、知青州。

translations.literal: He was punished for improperly authorizing the building of a fort at Baicao Plain at Linzhou, where prefectural generals including Wu Kan were defeated by Western Xia forces; he was again made Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture, Vice Minister of Revenue, and prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for improperly authorizing construction of a fort at Baicao Plain in Linzhou, where generals including Wu Kan were defeated by the Tangut forces; he was reduced to Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture, Vice Minister of Revenue, and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，不拜。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Left Department of the Ministry but did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Left Department of the Ministry but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 徙定州，召還京師，上章告老，尋以太子太保致仕，封潁國公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Dingzhou, recalled to the capital, submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and soon retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the title Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Dingzhou and then recalled to the capital, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and soon retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the title Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 薨，年七十六。

translations.literal: He died; he was seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗不豫，廢朝、臨奠皆不果，第遣使吊賻其家。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Renzong was ill; court sessions were suspended and the imperial condolence visit did not take place—only an envoy was sent with condolences and gifts to the family.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then ill; court sessions were suspended and no imperial condolence visit took place—only an envoy was sent with condolences and gifts to the family.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，加侍中，諡莊敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, given the additional title of Palace Attendant, and granted the posthumous designation Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works and Palace Attendant, with the posthumous name Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 籍曉律令，長於吏事。

translations.literal: Ji understood laws and regulations and excelled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was versed in laws and regulations and excelled in administrative matters.

sentences.zh: 持法深峭，軍中有犯，或斷斬刳磔，或累笞至死，以故士卒畏服。

translations.literal: His enforcement of law was severe and harsh; in the army, violators might be beheaded, dismembered, or flogged repeatedly until death—for this reason the soldiers feared and obeyed him.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law with brutal severity; in the army, offenders might be beheaded, dismembered, or flogged to death, and for this reason the soldiers feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 治民頗有惠愛，及為相，聲望減於治郡時。

translations.literal: In governing the people he showed considerable benevolence and care, but once he became chief councilor his reputation fell below what it had been when he governed prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the people he showed considerable kindness, but once he became chief councilor his standing fell below what it had been when he governed prefectures.

sentences.zh: 子：元英，朝散大夫。

translations.literal: His sons: Yuanying, Attendant Gentleman for Dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanying served as Attendant Gentleman for Dispersal.

sentences.zh: 孫：恭孫。

translations.literal: His grandson: Gongsun.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Gongsun.

sentences.zh: 孫 恭孫

translations.literal: Grandson Gongsun
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun

sentences.zh: 恭孫，字德孺，以蔭，補通判施州。

translations.literal: Gongsun, styled Deru, entered service by privilege and was appointed vice-prefect of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun, styled Deru, entered office by hereditary privilege as vice-prefect of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，部蠻向文強叛，詔轉運使王蘧領州事致討，恭孫說降文強而斬之。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era the tribal chieftain Xiang Wenqiang rebelled; an edict ordered transit commissioner Wang Sui to take charge of the prefecture and suppress him; Gongsun persuaded Wenqiang to surrender and then executed him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning era the tribal chieftain Xiang Wenqiang rebelled; transit commissioner Wang Sui was ordered to take charge of the prefecture and suppress him; Gongsun persuaded Wenqiang to surrender and then had him executed.

sentences.zh: 蘧上其功，進三秩，知涪州，遂以開邊為己任。

translations.literal: Sui reported his achievement; Gongsun was promoted three ranks, made prefect of Fuzhou, and thereafter took expanding the frontier as his personal mission.
translations.idiomatic: Sui reported the achievement; Gongsun was promoted three ranks and made prefect of Fuzhou, and from then on made frontier expansion his personal mission.

sentences.zh: 誘珍州駱文貴、承州駱世華納土，費不貲。

translations.literal: He induced Luo Wengui of Zhenzhou and Luo Shihua of Chengzhou to submit their territories, at enormous expense.
translations.idiomatic: He induced Luo Wengui of Zhenzhou and Luo Shihua of Chengzhou to submit their territories, at enormous cost.

sentences.zh: 轉運判官朱師古劾恭孫生事，詔黜師古而以恭孫代，於是溱、播、溪、思、費等州相繼降。

translations.literal: Transit deputy judge Zhu Shigu impeached Gongsun for provoking trouble; an edict dismissed Shigu and replaced him with Gongsun, and thereafter Qin, Bo, Xi, Si, and Fei prefectures surrendered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Transit deputy judge Zhu Shigu impeached Gongsun for stirring up trouble; the court dismissed Shigu and replaced him with Gongsun, and thereafter the prefectures of Qin, Bo, Xi, Si, and Fei surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 每開一城，輒褒遷，五年間，至徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: Each time a city was opened he was commended and promoted; within five years he reached Attendant Drafter of the Hall of Manifest Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a city was opened he was commended and promoted; within five years he rose to Attendant Drafter of the Hall of Manifest Worthies.

sentences.zh: 威州守乞通保、霸二州，進恭孫直學士、知成都府，委以招納。

translations.literal: The prefect of Weizhou requested opening communication with Bao and Ba prefectures; Gongsun was advanced to Direct Academician and made prefect of Chengdu, entrusted with recruitment and submission.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Weizhou petitioned to open communication with Bao and Ba prefectures; Gongsun was made Direct Academician and prefect of Chengdu and entrusted with winning over the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其酋董舜咨、董彥博來納土，詔遣赴闕，皆拜承宣使，賜第京師，更名保州祺州、霸州享州，使恭孫進築之。

translations.literal: Before long chieftains Dong Shunzi and Dong Yanbo came to submit their territories; an edict summoned them to court, both were appointed Both Commissioner Heralds and given residences in the capital; Bao Prefecture was renamed Qizhou and Ba Prefecture Xiangzhou, and Gongsun was ordered to advance and build them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long chieftains Dong Shunzi and Dong Yanbo submitted their territories; the court summoned them to the capital, made them Both Commissioner Heralds, and gave them residences in the capital; Bao Prefecture was renamed Qizhou and Ba Prefecture Xiangzhou, and Gongsun was ordered to advance construction.

sentences.zh: 言者論其貪縱，究治如章，謫保靜軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Critics charged him with greed and lax discipline; after investigation according to regulation he was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Baojing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged him with greed and lax discipline; after investigation as prescribed he was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Baojing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 才逾月，起知陳州，復待制，帥瀘州。

translations.literal: After barely a month he was reappointed prefect of Chenzhou, restored as Attendant Drafter, and made commander of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later he was reappointed prefect of Chenzhou, restored as Attendant Drafter, and made commander of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以築思州，進學士。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Academician for building Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Academician for constructing Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 前後在西南二十年，所得州縣，多張名簿，實瘠鹵不毛地，繕治轉餉，為蜀人病，無幾時皆廢。

translations.literal: Over twenty years in the southwest, the prefectures and counties he obtained were often inflated on the registers; in fact the land was barren and unproductive; maintaining and supplying them became a burden on the people of Shu, and before long most were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty years in the southwest, many of the prefectures and counties he gained existed only on paper; the land was in fact barren and unproductive, and maintaining and supplying them became a grievance for the people of Shu—before long most were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xuanhe era.

sentences.zh: 王隨，字子正，河南人。

translations.literal: Wang Sui, styled Zizheng, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, styled Zizheng, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 登進士甲科，為將作監丞、通判同州，遷秘書省著作郎、直史館、判三司磨勘司。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the top category, served as Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice-prefect of Tongzhou, and was promoted to Drafting Gentleman of the Secretariat, Corrector in the Historiography Office, and judge of the Fiscal Audits Bureau in the Directorate of Financial Planning.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the top category, served as Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice-prefect of Tongzhou, and was promoted to Drafting Gentleman of the Secretariat, Corrector in the Historiography Office, and judge of the Fiscal Audits Bureau.

sentences.zh: 為京西轉運副使，陛辭，且言曰：「臣父母家洛中，乃在所部，得奉湯藥，聖主之澤也。」

translations.literal: As deputy transit commissioner of the Jingxi Circuit, at his audience on departure he also said: "My parents' home is in Luoyang, which lies within my jurisdiction; I can attend to their medicine—this is the sovereign's grace."
translations.idiomatic: As deputy transit commissioner of the Jingxi Circuit, at his audience on departure he said, "My parents live in Luoyang, which falls within my jurisdiction, so I can attend to their medicine—this is the sovereign's grace."

sentences.zh: 真宗因賜詩寵行，以羊酒束帛令過家為壽。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong therefore bestowed a poem honoring his departure and sent wine, mutton, and silks for him to celebrate his parents' longevity when he passed home.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong therefore bestowed a poem honoring his departure and sent wine, mutton, and silks so he could celebrate his parents' longevity when he passed through home.

sentences.zh: 遷淮南轉運使，父憂，起復。

translations.literal: He was promoted to transit commissioner of Huainan; during mourning for his father he was recalled to service.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to transit commissioner of Huainan; when his father died he was recalled from mourning to resume office.

sentences.zh: 時歲比飢，隨敕屬部出庫錢，貸民市種糧，歲中約輸絹以償，流庸多復業。

translations.literal: Famine struck year after year; Sui ordered subordinate prefectures to release treasury funds, lend the people money to buy seed grain, and collect silk in repayment by midyear; many displaced persons returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck year after year; Sui ordered subordinate prefectures to release treasury funds, lend the people money to buy seed grain, and collect silk in repayment by midyear; many displaced persons returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 徙河東轉運使，三遷刑部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transit commissioner of Hedong, and thrice promoted to Outer Section Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice combined with Chief Censor for Miscellaneous Matters.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to transit commissioner of Hedong, he was thrice promoted to Outer Section Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice combined with Chief Censor for Miscellaneous Matters.

sentences.zh: 擢知制誥，以不善制辭，出知應天府。

translations.literal: He was selected as drafter of edicts but, failing at drafting formal prose, was sent out as prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as drafter of edicts but, being poor at drafting formal prose, was sent out as prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝謂宰相曰：「隨治南京太寬。」

translations.literal: One day the emperor said to the chief councilor: "Sui governs southern Nanjing too leniently."
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor told the chief councilor, "Sui governs southern Nanjing too leniently."

sentences.zh: 王旦曰：「南京，都會之地，隨臨事汗漫，無以彈壓」。

translations.literal: Wang Dan said: "Southern Nanjing is a great metropolitan center; Sui is lax in handling affairs and has no way to restrain the populace."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan said, "Southern Nanjing is a great metropolitan center; Sui is lax in handling affairs and cannot keep the populace in check."

sentences.zh: 改知揚州。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 再加右諫議大夫、權知開封府。

translations.literal: He was further made Right Remonstrating Grandee and given provisional charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Right Remonstrating Grandee with provisional charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為太子，拜右庶子，仍領府事。

translations.literal: When Renzong was crown prince, he was appointed Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent while continuing to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, Sui was made Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent while continuing to run the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周懷政誅，隨自陳嘗假懷政白金五十兩，奪知制誥，改給事中、知杭州。

translations.literal: After Zhou Huaizheng was executed, Sui voluntarily reported that he had once borrowed fifty taels of silver from Huaizheng; he was stripped of his draftership and made Supervising Censor and prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Huaizheng was executed, Sui voluntarily reported having borrowed fifty taels of silver from him; he was stripped of his draftership and made Supervising Censor and prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，復降秘書少監，徙通州。

translations.literal: At the start of the Qianxing era he was again demoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and transferred to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianxing era he was demoted again to Vice Director of the Secretariat and transferred to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以州少學者，徙孔子廟，起學舍，州人喜，遣子弟就學。

translations.literal: Because the prefecture had few scholars, he moved the Confucian temple, built schoolhouses, and the people rejoiced and sent their sons to study.
translations.idiomatic: Because the prefecture had few scholars, he relocated the Confucian temple, built schoolhouses, and the people rejoiced and sent their sons to study.

sentences.zh: 母喪，起復光祿卿、知潤州，徙江寧府。

translations.literal: After his mother died he was recalled from mourning to serve as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and prefect of Runzhou, then transferred to Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and prefect of Runzhou, then transferred to Jiangning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲大飢，轉運使移府發常平倉米，計口日給一升，隨置不聽，曰：「民所以飢者，由兼併閉糴，以邀高價也。」

translations.literal: During a great famine the transit commissioner ordered the prefecture to release ever-normal granary rice at one sheng per person per day; Sui refused, saying: "The reason the people are hungry is that magnates hoard grain and shut off sales to force high prices."
translations.idiomatic: During a severe famine the transit commissioner ordered the prefecture to release ever-normal granary rice at one sheng per person per day; Sui refused, saying, "The people are hungry because magnates hoard grain and shut off sales to force prices up."

sentences.zh: 乃大出官粟，平其價。

translations.literal: He then released a large quantity of government grain and stabilized the price.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he released a large quantity of government grain and stabilized the market price.

sentences.zh: 復給事中，為龍圖閣直學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: Restored as Supervising Censor, he became Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to Supervising Censor, he was made Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦卒有負罪逃入蕃部者，戎人輒奴畜之，小不如意，復執出求賞，前此坐法多死。

translations.literal: Qinzhou soldiers guilty of crimes who fled into tribal areas were often kept as slaves by the tribes; if displeased even slightly, they were handed back to seek reward; many had previously died under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou soldiers who fled into tribal areas after committing crimes were often kept as slaves by the tribes; if displeased even slightly, the tribes would hand them back to claim rewards, and many had previously been executed under the law.

sentences.zh: 隨下教能自歸者免死，聽復隸軍籍，由是多來歸者。

translations.literal: Sui issued an order that those who surrendered voluntarily would be spared death and allowed to re-enter the army rolls; for this reason many came back.
translations.idiomatic: Sui issued an order that those who surrendered voluntarily would be spared death and allowed to rejoin the army rolls, and many returned as a result.

sentences.zh: 又建請增蕃落卒，給廢陷馬地，募民耕種。

translations.literal: He also proposed increasing tribal frontier troops, granting abandoned lands lost to the enemy, and recruiting commoners to farm and plant.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed increasing tribal frontier troops, granting abandoned lands lost to the enemy, and recruiting farmers to cultivate them.

sentences.zh: 坐事，徙河南府。

translations.literal: For an offense he was transferred to Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for an offense, he was transferred to Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為御史中丞，同知禮部貢舉，遷尚書禮部侍郎、翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Censor-in-Chief, jointly supervised the Ministry of Rites examination, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and Hanlin Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Censor-in-Chief, jointly supervised the Ministry of Rites examination, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and Hanlin Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 明道中，為江淮安撫使，還拜戶部侍郎、參知政事，請與同列日獻前代名臣規諫一事。

translations.literal: In the Mingdao era he was Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai region; on return he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Vice Grand Councilor, and asked that he and his colleagues daily submit one case of remonstrance from famous ministers of past dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In the Mingdao era he served as Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai region; on returning he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Vice Grand Councilor, and asked that he and his colleagues submit one case of remonstrance from famous ministers of past dynasties each day.

sentences.zh: 議者謂非輔弼之職，其事遂寢。

translations.literal: Critics said this was not the duty of chief councillors, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said this was not the duty of chief councillors, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 加吏部侍郎、知樞密院事，為莊惠皇太后園陵監護使，拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事、昭文館大學士、監修國史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, made Supervisor of the tomb of Empress Dowager Zhuanghui, and appointed Vice Chief Councilor through the Menxia office, Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and overseer of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, made Supervisor of the tomb of Empress Dowager Zhuanghui, and appointed Vice Chief Councilor, Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and overseer of the national history.

sentences.zh: 自薛居正後，故事，初相無越遷門下侍郎者，學士丁度之失也。

translations.literal: Since Xue Juzheng there had been no precedent for a new chief councilor to skip directly to Vice Chief Councilor through the Menxia office—a lapse that began with Academician Ding Du.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xue Juzheng, precedent held that a new chief councilor should not skip directly to Vice Chief Councilor through the Menxia office—a lapse that began with Academician Ding Du.

sentences.zh: 隨外若方嚴，而治失於寬。

translations.literal: Outwardly Sui seemed upright and strict, yet in governance he erred on the side of leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Sui appeared upright and strict, yet in governing he erred on the side of leniency.

sentences.zh: 晚更卞急，輒嫚罵人。

translations.literal: In later years he grew more irascible and would casually revile people.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew more short-tempered and would casually revile people.

sentences.zh: 性喜佛，慕裴休之為人，然風跡弗逮也。

translations.literal: By nature he loved Buddhism and admired Pei Xiu's way of life, yet his conduct fell short of Pei's.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Buddhism by nature and admired Pei Xiu's way of life, yet his conduct fell short of Pei's.

sentences.zh: 章得象

translations.literal: Zhang Dexiang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dexiang.

sentences.zh: 章得象，字希言，世居泉州。

translations.literal: Zhang Dexiang, styled Xiyan, had lived for generations in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dexiang, styled Xiyan, was a native of Quanzhou for generations.

sentences.zh: 高祖仔鈞，事閩為建州刺史，遂家浦城。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zaijun served Min as prefect of Jianzhou, and the family then settled in Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zaijun served the Min regime as prefect of Jianzhou, and the family then settled in Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 得象母方娠，夢登山，遇神人授以玉象，及生，父奐復夢家庭積笏如山。

translations.literal: When Dexiang's mother was pregnant she dreamed of climbing a mountain and meeting a deity who gave her a jade elephant; when he was born, his father Huan again dreamed that the family courtyard was piled with tablets like a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: While Dexiang's mother was pregnant she dreamed of climbing a mountain and meeting a deity who gave her a jade elephant; when he was born, his father Huan dreamed that the family courtyard was piled with official tablets like a mountain.

sentences.zh: 長而好學，美姿表，為人莊重。

translations.literal: Growing up he loved learning, had a handsome appearance, and was grave in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he loved learning, was handsome in appearance, and carried himself with dignity.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，為大理評事、知玉山縣，遷本寺丞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Yushan County, and was promoted to Assistant Director of that court.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served as Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Yushan County, and was promoted to Assistant Director of the same court.

sentences.zh: 真宗將東封泰山，以殿中丞簽書兗州觀察判官事，知台州，歷南雄州，徙洪州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong was about to perform the eastern feng at Mount Tai, [Zhang Dexiang] was appointed Palace Attendant Attached Secretary signing Yanzhou Commissioner of Observation and Administration, governed Taizhou, served at Nanxiongzhou, and was transferred to Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong was preparing the eastern feng rites at Mount Tai, Dexiang was appointed attached secretary and signing commissioner of observation and administration for Yanzhou, then served as prefect of Taizhou, held office at Nanxiongzhou, and was transferred to Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊億以為有公輔器，薦之。

translations.literal: Yang Yi considered him to have the vessel of a chief minister and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi judged him fit for the highest office and put his name forward.

sentences.zh: 或問之，億曰：「閩士輕狹，而章公深厚有容，此其貴也。」

translations.literal: When someone asked about this, Yi said: "Men from Min are light and narrow-minded, whereas Duke Zhang is deep and magnanimous—this is why he will rise to eminence."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Yi replied: "Scholars from Min tend to be shallow and petty, but Duke Zhang is steady and broad-minded—that is what will carry him to the top."

sentences.zh: 得象嘗與億戲博李宗諤家，一夕負錢三十萬，而酣寢自如。

translations.literal: Dexiang once played gambling games with Yi at Li Zong'e's home; in one night he lost three hundred thousand coins, yet slept soundly as if nothing had happened.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang once gambled with Yi at Li Zong'e's house and lost three hundred thousand cash in a single night, yet slept deeply and untroubled.

sentences.zh: 他日博勝，得宗諤金一奩；

translations.literal: Another day when he won at gambling, he took from Zong'e one golden casket;
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he won and took a gold casket from Zong'e;

sentences.zh: 數日博又負，即反奩與宗諤，封識未嘗發也。

translations.literal: A few days later when he lost again at gambling, he immediately returned the casket to Zong'e—the seals had never been broken.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he lost again and at once returned the casket to Zong'e without ever having broken the seal.

sentences.zh: 其度量宏廓如此。

translations.literal: His breadth of mind was so grand.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the largeness of his temperament.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召試，為直史館、安撫京東，權三司度支判官，累遷尚書刑部郎中，使契丹，遂以兵部郎中知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned for examination and appointed Direct Historian in the Historiography Office, Pacification Commissioner of the eastern capital circuit, acting Bureau Judge in the Ministry of Revenue of the Three Bureaus; he was repeatedly promoted to Aide in the Bureau of Punishments in the Ministry of Justice; was sent as envoy to the Khitan; and then was appointed Grand Secretary as Aide in the Bureau of War in the Ministry of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was summoned for examination, made a direct historian, appointed pacification commissioner for the eastern capital region, and given acting charge of revenue affairs in the Three Bureaus. He rose through repeated promotions to aide in the Bureau of Punishments, served as envoy to the Khitan, and was then appointed grand secretary with the rank of aide in the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 逾年，為翰林學士，遷右諫議大夫，以給事中為群牧使，遷禮部侍郎兼龍圖閣學士，進承旨兼侍講學士，擢同知樞密院事，遷戶部侍郎，遂拜同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。
