translations.literal: After a year he became Hanlin Academician; was promoted to Right Remonstrance Councillor; served as Supervisor of Censorate as Commissioner of Pasturage Administration; was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Academician in the Hall of Dragon Diagrams; advanced to Senior Academician and concurrently Lecturing Academician; was elevated to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue; and then was appointed Grand Councillor under the Secretariat-Chancellery and Grand Academician in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he entered the Hanlin Academy, rose to right remonstrance councillor, served as commissioner of pasturage administration while holding the post of supervisor of the censorate, became vice minister of rites and an academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, advanced to senior academician and lecturing academician, was elevated to vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, promoted to vice minister of revenue, and finally appointed grand councillor and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 帝謂得象曰：「向者太后臨朝，群臣邪正，朕皆默識之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Dexiang: "When the Empress Dowager previously held court, I silently noted which ministers were upright and which corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Dexiang: "While the Empress Dowager ruled from behind the screen, I kept silent tally of who among the ministers was loyal and who was not.

sentences.zh: 卿清忠無所附，且未嘗有所干請，今日用卿，職此也。」

translations.literal: You are upright and loyal and attach yourself to no faction, and you have never made personal requests. That is why I appoint you today."
translations.idiomatic: You are honest, loyal, and beholden to no clique, and you have never come to me with private requests. That is why I am elevating you now."

sentences.zh: 陝西用兵，加中書侍郎兼工部尚書兼樞密使，辭所加官。

translations.literal: When military operations were launched in Shaanxi, he was given the additional titles of Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Works, and Commissioner of Military Affairs, but declined the additional offices.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Shaanxi, he was offered the additional posts of vice director of the Secretariat, minister of works, and commissioner of military affairs, but declined the extra titles.

sentences.zh: 明年，以工部尚書為昭文館大學士。

translations.literal: The next year, as Minister of Works he became Grand Academician in the Hall of Broad Culture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made grand academician of the Hall of Broad Culture while retaining the title of minister of works.

sentences.zh: 慶歷五年，拜鎮安軍節度使、同平章事，封郇國公，徙判河南府，守司空致仕，薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qingli, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhen'an Army and Concurrent Grand Councillor, enfeoffed as Duke of Xun, transferred to serve as Administrator of Henan Prefecture, retired with the honorary rank of Minister of Works, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Qingli era he was appointed military commissioner of Zhen'an Army and concurrent grand councillor, enfeoffed as Duke of Xun, transferred to administer Henan Prefecture, retired with the honorary rank of minister of works, and died.

sentences.zh: 故事，致仕官乘輿不臨奠，帝特往焉。

translations.literal: By precedent the imperial carriage did not attend funeral rites for retired officials, but the Emperor went in person.
translations.idiomatic: Custom held that the emperor did not attend the funerals of retired officials, but on this occasion he went himself.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉兼侍中，諡文憲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Commander and concurrent Palace Attendant; his posthumous title was Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand commander and palace attendant, with the posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，改諡文簡。

translations.literal: During Huangyou his posthumous title was changed to Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangyou era his posthumous name was revised to Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 得象在翰林十二年，章獻太后臨朝，宦官方熾，太后每遣內侍至學士院，得象必正色待之，或不交一言。

translations.literal: Dexiang served in the Hanlin Academy for twelve years. When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held court, eunuch officials were at the height of their power; whenever the Empress Dowager sent palace attendants to the Academy, Dexiang always received them with stern formality and sometimes did not exchange a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang spent twelve years in the Hanlin Academy. Under Empress Dowager Zhangxian, eunuch power was at its peak, and whenever she sent palace attendants to the academy, Dexiang met them with cold formality and sometimes refused to speak at all.

sentences.zh: 在中書凡八年，宗黨親戚，一切抑而不進。

translations.literal: During his eight years in the Secretariat altogether, he held back all clansmen and relatives and would not advance any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his eight years in the chief secretariat he blocked every kinsman and relation from promotion.

sentences.zh: 仁宗銳意天下事，進用韓琦、范仲淹、富弼，使同得象經畫當世急務，得象無所建明，御史孫抗數言之，得象居位自若。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was intent on affairs under Heaven and promoted Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi, appointing them together with Dexiang to plan pressing matters of the age; Dexiang offered no proposals for improvement. Censor Sun Kang spoke of this repeatedly, yet Dexiang remained in office as calmly as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong threw himself into governing the realm and elevated Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi, setting them with Dexiang to chart the urgent business of the day. Dexiang contributed nothing. Censor Sun Kang raised the point again and again, but Dexiang sat in office unruffled.

sentences.zh: 既而章十上請罷，帝不得已，許之。

translations.literal: Before long he memorialized ten times requesting dismissal; the Emperor, unable to refuse, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually submitted ten memorials asking to be relieved; the Emperor, left no choice, consented.

sentences.zh: 初，閩人謠曰：「南臺江合出宰相。」

translations.literal: Long ago the people of Min had a song: "When the Nantai River joins, a chief minister will emerge."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, the people of Min had a saying: "When the Nantai River flows together, a chief minister will appear."

sentences.zh: 至得象相時，沙涌可涉云。

translations.literal: When Dexiang became chief minister, it was said, people could wade through the sandbanks.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Dexiang reached the chief ministership, it was said, one could wade across the sandbanks where the rivers met.

sentences.zh: 論曰：殊、籍、隨、得象皆起孤生，致位宰相。

translations.literal: The historians comment: Shu, Ji, Sui, and Dexiang all rose from solitary beginnings to reach the position of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The historians observe: Shu, Ji, Sui, and Dexiang all rose from humble, isolated origins to the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 籍通曉法令，隨練習民事，皆能用其所長。

translations.literal: Ji was thoroughly versed in statutes and ordinances; Sui was practiced in civilian administration—each was able to apply his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Ji mastered law and regulation; Sui was seasoned in civil affairs—each put his particular gifts to use.

sentences.zh: 然籍終至絀免，隨數遭譴斥，何其才之難得也。

translations.literal: Yet Ji was ultimately demoted and dismissed, and Sui was repeatedly censured and expelled—how hard it is to retain such talent!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ji ended in demotion and removal, and Sui was rebuked and cast out again and again—how difficult it is to keep such talent in place!

sentences.zh: 得象渾厚有容，殊喜薦拔人物，樂善不倦，方之諸人，殊其最優乎！

translations.literal: Dexiang was magnanimous and tolerant; Shu delighted in recommending and advancing men, tireless in doing good—compared with the others, was Shu not the finest?
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang was steady and broad-minded; Shu loved discovering and promoting talent and never tired of doing good. Among them all, was Shu not the best?

sentences.zh: 呂夷簡

translations.literal: Lu Yijian
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yijian

sentences.zh: 呂夷簡，字坦夫，先世萊州人。

translations.literal: Lu Yijian, styled Tanfu, was by ancestry a native of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yijian, styled Tanfu, came from a Laizhou family.

sentences.zh: 祖龜祥知壽州，子孫遂為壽州人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guixiang served as prefect of Shouzhou, and thereafter his descendants became natives of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guixiang governed Shouzhou, and from then on the family counted itself among the people of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夷簡進士及第，補絳州軍事推官，稍遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: Yijian passed the jinshi examination and was appointed military administrative assistant in Jiangzhou; he was gradually promoted to Vice Director in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian passed the jinshi examination, took up a military administrative post in Jiangzhou, and was gradually promoted to vice director in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 祥符中，試材識兼茂明於體用科，或言六科所以求闕政，今封禪告成，何闕政之求，罷之。

translations.literal: During Xiangfu he was examined in the "Abundant Talent and Thorough Discernment, Clear in Substance and Use" special degree category. Someone said the six special categories were meant to seek out deficiencies in government; now that the feng and shan rites had been completed, what deficiencies were there to seek—so the category was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiangfu era he was tested in the special "Abundant Talent, Clear in Substance and Use" category. Critics argued that the six special examinations existed to expose flaws in government, and that with the feng and shan rites already completed there was nothing left to expose—so the category was abolished.

sentences.zh: 通判通州，徙濠州，再遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He served as vice prefect of Tongzhou, was transferred to Haozhou, and was again promoted to Erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Tongzhou, was moved to Haozhou, and was later promoted to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 河北水，選知濱州。

translations.literal: Flooding in Hebei led to his selection as prefect of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After floods struck Hebei, he was chosen to govern Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 代還奏：「農器有算，非所以勸力本也。」

translations.literal: On returning from his replacement tour he memorialized: "There are calculated taxes on farm implements—this is not the way to encourage the foundation of agricultural labor."
translations.idiomatic: When his tour of duty ended and he returned to court, he memorialized: "Taxing farm tools is no way to encourage people to work the land."

sentences.zh: 遂詔天下農器皆勿算。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued that farm implements throughout the empire should not be taxed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed exempting farm implements from taxation throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 擢提點兩浙刑獄，遷尚書祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Judicial Intendant for the two Zhe circuits and promoted to Assistant Director in the Bureau of Shrines in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial intendant for the two Zhe circuits and then to assistant director in the Bureau of Shrines.

sentences.zh: 時京師大建宮觀，伐材木於南方。

translations.literal: At the time the capital was undertaking massive construction of palaces and Daoist temples, and timber was being harvested in the south.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was then in the midst of a vast building campaign of palaces and temples, and timber was being cut in the south.

sentences.zh: 有司責期會，工徒至有死者，誣以亡命，收繫妻子。

translations.literal: The relevant offices enforced deadlines; some laborers even died. [Officials] falsely charged them with desertion and seized and imprisoned their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Officials pressed hard for deadlines; some laborers died. They were falsely accused of desertion, and their wives and children were seized and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 夷簡請緩其役，從之。

translations.literal: Yijian requested that the corvée labor be eased; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian asked that the labor be eased, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「盛冬挽運艱苦，須河流漸通，以卒番送。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Transport by hauling in deep winter is extremely arduous. We should wait until the rivers gradually become passable, then have the soldiers relay the shipments in rotations."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Hauling timber in the depths of winter is brutal. Wait until the rivers open, then rotate soldiers to relay the loads downstream."

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「觀卿奏，有為國愛民之心矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said: "Reading your memorial, I see you have a mind devoted to serving the state and caring for the people."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said: "From your memorial I can see a heart that serves the state and cares for the people."

sentences.zh: 擢刑部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Director in the Bureau of Punishments and concurrently served as Attending Imperial Censor with responsibility for mixed affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director in the Bureau of Punishments and given concurrent charge of mixed censorial affairs.

sentences.zh: 蜀賊李順叛，執送闕下，左右稱賀。

translations.literal: When the Sichuan bandit Li Shun rebelled, [someone] captured and sent [a prisoner] to the capital; those around the Emperor offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sichuan rebel Li Shun rose in revolt, a captive was brought to the capital and the courtiers around the emperor broke into congratulation.

sentences.zh: 既而屬御史臺按之，非是，賀者趣具順獄，夷簡曰：「是可欺朝廷邪？」

translations.literal: Subsequently the Censorate was assigned to investigate and found it was not [Li Shun]. Those who had congratulated urged that Li Shun's case be hurriedly completed. Yijian said: "Can one deceive the court in this way?"
translations.idiomatic: The censorate was then ordered to investigate and found the man was not Li Shun. Those who had celebrated pressed to close Li Shun's case anyway. Yijian said: "Are we to deceive the throne?"

sentences.zh: 卒以實奏，忤大臣意。

translations.literal: In the end he reported according to the facts, offending the wishes of a senior minister.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the truth in the end, to the displeasure of a senior minister.

sentences.zh: 歲蝗旱，夷簡請責躬修政，嚴飭輔相，思所以共順天意；

translations.literal: In a year of locust plague and drought, Yijian requested that the Emperor examine himself and reform government, strictly discipline the chief ministers, and consider how jointly to accord with Heaven's will;
translations.idiomatic: In a year of locusts and drought, Yijian urged the emperor to examine his own conduct, tighten discipline among the chief ministers, and seek ways together to align with Heaven's intent;

sentences.zh: 及奏彈李溥專利罔上。

translations.literal: and also submitted an impeachment of Li Po for monopolizing profit and deceiving the throne.
translations.idiomatic: and he also impeached Li Po for hoarding profit and misleading the throne.

sentences.zh: 寇準判永興，黥有罪者徙湖南，道由京師，上準變事。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun was administering Yongxing; he tattooed and banished a criminal to Hunan. When the man passed through the capital, someone reported to the throne that Kou Zhun was plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: While Kou Zhun was administering Yongxing, he tattooed and exiled a convict to Hunan. When the man passed through the capital, someone reported that Kou Zhun was plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 夷簡曰：「準治下急，是欲中傷準爾，宜勿問，益徙之遠方。」

translations.literal: Yijian said: "Kou Zhun governs his subordinates harshly. This is merely an attempt to slander Zhun. We should not investigate it, and instead exile the man even farther away."
translations.idiomatic: Yijian said: "Kou Zhun runs a tight hand. This is simply an attempt to ruin him. Do not pursue it; send the man even farther into exile instead."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The suggestion was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 趙安仁為御史中丞，夷簡以親嫌，改起居舍人、同勾當通進司兼銀臺封駁事。

translations.literal: When Zhao Anren became Imperial Censor-in-Chief, Yijian, because of kinship, was transferred to Diarist in the Palace Secretariat and concurrently served in the Document Transmission Office with responsibility for memorial review at the Silver Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Anren became imperial censor-in-chief, Yijian was moved to diarist in the palace secretariat because of a family connection, and given concurrent charge of document transmission and memorial review at the Silver Terrace.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，還，知制誥。

translations.literal: He served as envoy to the Khitan; on his return he was appointed Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as envoy to the Khitan, he returned and was appointed grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 兩川飢，為安撫使，進龍圖閣直學士，再遷刑部郎中、權知開封府。

translations.literal: When the two Chuan circuits suffered famine, he was appointed Pacification Commissioner; advanced to Direct Academician in the Hall of Dragon Diagrams; and was again promoted to Aide in the Bureau of Punishments and acting Administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the two Chuan circuits, he was made pacification commissioner, promoted to direct academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, and later rose to aide in the Bureau of Punishments with acting charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治嚴辦有聲，帝識姓名於屏風，將大用之。

translations.literal: His governance was strict and efficient and won renown; the Emperor noted his name on a folding screen and intended to give him major appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was rigorous and won wide notice; the emperor wrote his name on a folding screen, intending to promote him to high office.

sentences.zh: 天聖末，加中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Tiansheng era he was given the additional title of Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tiansheng era he was made vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 章懿太后為順容，薨，宮中未治喪，夷簡朝奏事，因曰：「聞有宮嬪亡者。」

translations.literal: Empress Zhangyi had been an Honored Consort; she died, but the palace had not yet arranged mourning. During court Yijian reported on affairs and added: "I have heard that a palace consort has died."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangyi, formerly an honored consort, had died, but the palace had not yet begun mourning rites. At court Yijian reported on business and added, "I have heard that a palace lady has passed away."

sentences.zh: 太后矍然曰：「宰相亦預宮中事邪？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager started in alarm and said: "Does the chief minister also involve himself in palace affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager started and said, "Does the chief minister now meddle in palace affairs too?"

sentences.zh: 引帝偕起。

translations.literal: She took the Emperor and rose together [with him].
translations.idiomatic: She took the emperor by the hand and rose with him.

sentences.zh: 有頃獨出，曰：「卿何間我母子也？」

translations.literal: After a short while she came out alone and said: "Why do you come between mother and son?"
translations.idiomatic: A moment later she came out alone and said, "Why do you drive a wedge between mother and son?"

sentences.zh: 夷簡曰：「太后他日不欲全劉氏乎？」

translations.literal: Yijian said: "Does not the Empress Dowager wish in future to preserve the Liu house intact?"
translations.idiomatic: Yijian replied, "Does Your Majesty not wish, in days to come, to preserve the Liu house whole?"

sentences.zh: 太后意稍解。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's mind was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's anger eased a little.

sentences.zh: 有司希太后旨，言歲月葬未利。

translations.literal: The relevant offices, seeking to flatter the Empress Dowager's intent, said the dates were inauspicious for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The officials, eager to please the empress dowager, claimed the calendar offered no auspicious day for burial.

sentences.zh: 夷簡請發哀成服，備儀仗葬之。

translations.literal: Yijian requested that mourning be declared and full garments of mourning be worn, and that she be buried with full ceremony and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian asked that public mourning be declared, that the court don full mourning garments, and that she be buried with full ceremonial escort.

sentences.zh: 大內火，百官晨朝，而宮門不開。

translations.literal: A fire broke out within the Inner Palace; the hundred officials came for morning audience, but the palace gates did not open.
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out in the inner palace. The officials arrived for the morning audience, but the palace gates remained shut.

sentences.zh: 輔臣請對，帝御拱辰門，百官拜樓下，夷簡獨不拜。

translations.literal: The chief ministers requested an audience; the Emperor took his place at the Gongchen Gate; the hundred officials bowed below the tower—Yijian alone did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers asked for an audience. The emperor appeared at the Gongchen Gate; the officials bowed from below the tower, but Yijian alone refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 帝使人問其故，曰：「宮庭有變，群臣願一望清光。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent someone to ask the reason. He said: "There has been a disturbance in the palace; the ministers wish but one glance at Your clear countenance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent someone to ask why. Yijian said, "There has been trouble in the palace. The ministers beg only to see Your Majesty's face."

sentences.zh: 帝舉簾見之，乃拜。

translations.literal: The Emperor raised the screen and showed himself; only then did [Yijian] bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lifted the curtain and showed himself; only then did Yijian bow.

sentences.zh: 詔以為修大內使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Commissioner for Reconstruction of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him commissioner for rebuilding the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 內成，進尚書右僕射兼門下侍郎，辭僕射，乃兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the inner construction was completed, he was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery; he declined the vice directorship and instead held the concurrent post of Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner palace was finished, he was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent vice director of the Chancellery. He declined the vice directorship and accepted concurrent appointment as minister of personnel instead.

sentences.zh: 初，荊王子養禁中，既長，夷簡請出之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Prince of Jing's son had been raised within the Forbidden City; when he had grown up, Yijian requested that he be sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Jing's son had been raised inside the palace. Once he came of age, Yijian asked that he be sent out.

sentences.zh: 太后欲留使從帝誦讀，夷簡曰：「上富春秋，所親非儒學之臣，恐無益聖德。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to keep him so he might attend the Emperor in study and recitation. Yijian said: "Your Majesty is still in the spring of youth; those close to you are not men of classical learning—I fear this will not benefit your sacred virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wanted to keep him to attend the emperor in study. Yijian said, "Your Majesty is still young. Those close to you are not scholars of the classics, and I fear that will do your virtue no good."

sentences.zh: 即日命還邸中。

translations.literal: That very day an order sent him back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an order sent him back to his own residence.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，帝始親政事，夷簡手疏陳八事，曰：正朝綱，塞邪徑，禁貨賂，辨佞壬，絕女謁，疏近習，罷力役，節冗費。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager died, the Emperor at last personally handled government affairs. Yijian submitted a handwritten memorial setting forth eight matters: rectifying court discipline; blocking corrupt paths; banning bribery; distinguishing sycophants; cutting off female petitions; keeping at a distance intimate favorites; abolishing forced labor; and cutting wasteful expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, the emperor at last took up government himself. Yijian submitted a handwritten memorial listing eight reforms: restore court discipline, close corrupt channels, forbid bribery, distinguish flatterers, cut off women's petitions at court, keep favored intimates at arm's length, end forced labor, and trim wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 其勸帝語甚切。

translations.literal: His words of advice to the Emperor were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel to the emperor was blunt and urgent.

sentences.zh: 帝始與夷簡謀，以張耆、夏竦皆太后所任用者也，悉罷之，退告郭皇后。

translations.literal: The Emperor at first consulted with Yijian and, because Zhang Qi and Xia Song were both men the Empress Dowager had employed, dismissed them all; afterward he told Empress Guo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first plotted with Yijian to dismiss Zhang Qi and Xia Song, both appointees of the empress dowager, and afterward told Empress Guo.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「夷簡獨不附太后邪？

translations.literal: The Empress said: "Was Yijian alone not attached to the Empress Dowager?
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "Do you think Yijian alone stood apart from the empress dowager?

sentences.zh: 但多機巧、善應變耳。」

translations.literal: He merely has many stratagems and is skilled at adapting to change."
translations.idiomatic: He is simply clever and good at shifting with the moment."

sentences.zh: 由是夷簡亦罷為武勝軍節度使、檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事、判陳州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yijian was also dismissed and made Military Commissioner of Wusheng Army, Acting Grand Tutor, Concurrent Grand Councillor under the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Administrator of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On that account Yijian was dismissed as well and made military commissioner of Wusheng Army, acting grand tutor, concurrent grand councillor, and administrator of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 及宣制，夷簡方押班，聞唱名，大駭，不知其故。

translations.literal: When the edict was proclaimed, Yijian was just leading the ranks in formation; hearing his name announced, he was greatly alarmed and did not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was read out, Yijian was still leading the court in formation. Hearing his own name called, he was stunned and had no idea why.

sentences.zh: 而夷簡素厚內侍副都知閻文應，因使為中詗，久之，乃知事由皇后也。

translations.literal: Yijian had long been on close terms with Yan Wenying, Deputy Director of Inner Attendants; he therefore had him spy from within. After a long time he finally learned that the affair originated with the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian had long been close to Yan Wenying, deputy director of inner attendants, and sent him to inquire inside the palace. Only after some time did he learn that the empress was behind it.

sentences.zh: 歲中而夷簡復相。

translations.literal: Within the year Yijian was again chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year Yijian was back in the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 初，劉渙上疏請太后還政，太后怒，使投嶺外，屬太后疾革，夷簡請留之。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Huan had submitted a memorial requesting that the Empress Dowager return power; the Empress Dowager was angry and had him sent beyond the mountain passes. When the Empress Dowager's illness grew critical, Yijian requested that he be kept back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Huan had memorialized asking the empress dowager to return power to the emperor. She was furious and had him sent beyond the passes. When her illness turned grave, Yijian asked that Liu be kept from exile.

sentences.zh: 至是，渙以前疏自言，帝擢渙右正言，顧謂夷簡：「向者樞密院亟欲投渙，賴卿以免。」

translations.literal: At this point Huan spoke of his earlier memorial himself; the Emperor elevated Huan to Right Rectifier and, turning to Yijian, said: "Earlier the Bureau of Military Affairs was eager to send Huan into exile beyond the passes; thanks to you he was spared."
translations.idiomatic: Now Huan spoke up about his old memorial, and the emperor promoted him to right rectifier. Turning to Yijian, he said, "The Bureau of Military Affairs was ready to banish Liu Huan. It was thanks to you that he was spared."

sentences.zh: 夷簡謝，因曰：「渙由疏外故敢言，大臣或及此，則太后必疑風旨自陛下，使子母不相安矣。」

translations.literal: Yijian thanked him and added: "Huan dared to speak because he was far removed [from court]; had a chief minister done so, the Empress Dowager would surely have suspected that such sentiment came from Your Majesty, and mother and son would not have lived at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Yijian thanked him and added, "Huan spoke because he was far from court. Had a chief minister said the same, the empress dowager would have suspected the words came from you, and peace between mother and son would have been impossible."

sentences.zh: 帝以夷簡為忠。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered Yijian loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as proof of Yijian's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 郭后以怒尚美人，批其頰，誤傷帝頸。

translations.literal: Empress Guo, in anger at the Honored Beauty Shang, struck her on the cheek and accidentally injured the Emperor's neck.
translations.idiomatic: In anger at the Honored Beauty Shang, Empress Guo struck her on the cheek and accidentally scratched the emperor's neck.

sentences.zh: 帝以爪痕示執政大臣，夷簡以前罷相故，遂主廢后議。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed the scratch marks to the chief ministers. Because Yijian had previously been dismissed from the chief ministership, he now led the argument to depose the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the scratch to the chief ministers. Because Yijian had once been removed from office himself, he now led the push to depose the empress.

sentences.zh: 仁宗疑之，夷簡曰：「光武，漢之明主也，郭后止以怨懟坐廢，況傷陛下頸乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong hesitated. Yijian said: "Emperor Guangwu of Han was an enlightened ruler; Empress Guo was deposed merely for resentment and complaint—how much more when the Empress has injured Your Majesty's neck?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong hesitated. Yijian said, "Emperor Guangwu of Han was an enlightened ruler, yet he deposed Empress Guo merely for resentment and complaint. How much more when she has injured Your Majesty's neck?"

sentences.zh: 夷簡將廢后，先敕有司，無得受臺諫章奏。

translations.literal: As Yijian prepared to depose the Empress, he first issued orders to the relevant offices that they were not to accept memorials from the censorate and remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: As Yijian moved to depose the empress, he first ordered the relevant offices not to accept memorials from the censorate and remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 於是御史中丞孔道輔、右司諫范仲淹率臺諫詣閤門請對，有旨令臺諫詣中書，夷簡乃貶出道輔等，后遂廢。

translations.literal: Thereupon Imperial Censor-in-Chief Kong Daofu and Right Remonstrance Official Fan Zhongyan led the censorate and remonstrance officials to the Gate of Audience to request an audience. An edict directed them to go to the Secretariat; Yijian then demoted and expelled Daofu and the others, and the Empress was finally deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial censor-in-chief Kong Daofu and right remonstrance official Fan Zhongyan then led the censorate and remonstrance corps to the Gate of Audience to request an audience. An edict sent them instead to the Secretariat, where Yijian demoted and expelled Daofu and the rest. The empress was deposed.

sentences.zh: 宗室子益眾，為置大宗正糾率，增教授員。

translations.literal: As imperial clansmen grew ever more numerous, a Chief Overseer of the Imperial Clan was established to maintain discipline, and the number of instructors was increased.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial clansmen multiplied, a chief overseer of the imperial clan was appointed to keep order, and more instructors were added.

sentences.zh: 加右僕射，封申國公。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Right Vice Director and enfeoffed as Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right vice director and enfeoffed as Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 王曾與夷簡數爭事，不平，曾斥夷簡納賂市恩。

translations.literal: Wang Zeng frequently disputed affairs with Yijian and was displeased; Zeng accused Yijian of accepting bribes and currying favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng quarreled with Yijian repeatedly and grew resentful; he accused Yijian of taking bribes and trading favors.

sentences.zh: 夷簡乞置對，帝問曾，曾語屈，於是二人皆罷。

translations.literal: Yijian requested a face-to-face confrontation before the throne. The Emperor questioned Zeng; Zeng's words faltered—whereupon both men were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian asked for a direct confrontation before the throne. The emperor questioned Wang Zeng, whose answers faltered, and both men were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 夷簡以鎮安軍節度使、同平章事判許州，徙天雄軍。

translations.literal: Yijian served as Military Commissioner of Zhen'an Army and Concurrent Grand Councillor administering Xuzhou, then was transferred to Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian was sent out as military commissioner of Zhen'an Army and concurrent grand councillor administering Xuzhou, then transferred to Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以右僕射復入相，逾年，進位司空，辭不拜，徙許國公。

translations.literal: Before long he reentered the chief ministership as Right Vice Director. After a year he was promoted to Minister of Works; he declined to accept the appointment and was transferred to Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to the chief ministership as right vice director. A year later he was offered minister of works; he declined the appointment and was made Duke of Xu instead.

sentences.zh: 時方飭兵備，以判樞密院事，而諫官田況言總判名太重，改兼樞密使。

translations.literal: At the time military readiness was being tightened; he was given charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs as its overall administrator, but Remonstrance Official Tian Kuang said the title of overall administrator was too weighty, so he was changed to Concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then tightening military readiness and gave him overall charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but remonstrance official Tian Kuang argued the title was too grand, so he was made concurrent commissioner of military affairs instead.

sentences.zh: 契丹聚兵幽薊，聲言將入寇，議者請城洛陽。

translations.literal: The Khitan massed troops at You and Ji, proclaiming they would invade; some in council proposed fortifying Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan massed troops around You and Ji and declared they would invade. Some at court proposed fortifying Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 夷簡謂：「契丹畏壯侮怯，遽城洛陽，亡以示威，景德之役，非乘輿濟河，則契丹未易服也。

translations.literal: Yijian said: "The Khitan respect strength and despise timidity. Hurriedly fortifying Luoyang would show no display of power. In the Jingde campaign, had the imperial carriage not crossed the river, the Khitan would not easily have submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian said, "The Khitan respect strength and despise weakness. Rushing to fortify Luoyang would show no sign of resolve. In the Jingde campaign, had the emperor not crossed the river in person, the Khitan would never have submitted so readily.

sentences.zh: 宜建都大名，示將親征以伐其謀。」

translations.literal: It would be fitting to establish the capital at Daming, showing intent to take the field in person to thwart their designs."
translations.idiomatic: We should make Daming our capital and signal that the emperor intends to lead the campaign in person, thereby foiling their plans."

sentences.zh: 或曰：「此虛聲爾，不若修洛陽。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "This is mere empty bluster; better to repair Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected, "That would be empty bluster. It would be better to fortify Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 夷簡曰：「此子囊城郢計也。

translations.literal: Yijian said: "This is Zinang's plan of fortifying Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian replied, "That is the same stratagem as when Zinang walled in Ying.

sentences.zh: 使契丹得渡河，雖高城深池，何可恃耶？」

translations.literal: If the Khitan are allowed to cross the river, though walls be high and moats deep, what can be relied upon?"
translations.idiomatic: If we let the Khitan cross the river, no high walls or deep moats will save us."

sentences.zh: 乃建北京。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Northern Capital was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Capital was then established.

sentences.zh: 未幾，感風眩，詔拜司空、平章軍國重事，疾稍間，命數日一至中書，裁決可否。

translations.literal: Before long he suffered wind dizziness; an edict appointed him Minister of Works and Grand Councillor for State and Military Affairs. When his illness eased somewhat, he was ordered to come to the Secretariat every few days to decide what should and should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was stricken with vertigo. An edict made him minister of works and grand councillor for state and military affairs. When he improved slightly, he was ordered to visit the Secretariat every few days to pass judgment on pending affairs.

sentences.zh: 夷簡力辭，復降手詔曰：「古謂髭可療疾，今翦以賜卿。」

translations.literal: Yijian firmly declined. Another hand edict was issued: "The ancients said beard can cure illness; now it is clipped and bestowed upon you."
translations.idiomatic: Yijian strongly declined. The emperor then sent a personal note: "The ancients held that a beard could cure illness. I have had mine trimmed and am sending it to you."

sentences.zh: 三年春，帝御延和殿召見，敕乘馬至殿門，命內侍取兀子輿以前。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year the Emperor held court in the Yanhe Hall to summon him, ordering him to ride a horse to the hall gate and commanding eunuch attendants to fetch a sedan chair to carry him forward.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the emperor received him in the Yanhe Hall, ordered him to ride as far as the hall gate, and had attendants bring a sedan chair to carry him the rest of the way.

sentences.zh: 夷簡引避久之，詔給扶毋拜。

translations.literal: Yijian withdrew and declined for a long time; an edict granted him support and exempted him from bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian long refused to approach. An edict granted him attendants to lean on and excused him from bowing.

sentences.zh: 乃授司徒、監修國史，軍國大事與中書、樞密同議。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Minister over the Masses and Supervisor of the compilation of the National History; major state and military affairs were deliberated jointly with the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made minister over the masses and supervisor of the national history, with major state and military affairs to be decided jointly with the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 固請老，以太尉致仕，朝朔望。

translations.literal: He firmly requested retirement; he was granted retirement as Minister of War and attended court on the first and fifteenth of each month.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed hard for retirement and was granted it as minister of war, with permission to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 既薨，帝見群臣，涕下，曰：「安得憂國忘身如夷簡者！」

translations.literal: After he died, when the Emperor met the assembled ministers, tears fell as he said: "How can we find another who cares for the state and forgets himself like Yijian!"
translations.idiomatic: After his death, facing the assembled ministers, the emperor wept and said, "Where will we find another who cares for the realm and forgets himself as Yijian did?"

sentences.zh: 贈太師、中書令，諡文靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat; his posthumous title was Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 自仁宗初立，太后臨朝十餘年，天下晏然，夷簡之力為多。

translations.literal: From when Emperor Renzong first ascended the throne, the Empress Dowager held court for more than ten years and the realm remained tranquil; Yijian's efforts contributed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of Emperor Renzong's reign, while the empress dowager governed for more than ten years and the realm stayed at peace, Yijian's role was large.

sentences.zh: 其後元昊反，四方久不用兵，師出數敗；

translations.literal: Afterwards Yuan Hao rebelled; throughout the realm arms had long lain idle; when armies went forth they suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yuan Hao rebelled, the empire had long gone without war, and the armies sent against him were repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 契丹乘之，遣使求關南地。

translations.literal: The Khitan seized the opportunity and sent envoys to demand the lands south of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan took advantage of the crisis and sent envoys demanding the territory south of the pass.

sentences.zh: 頗賴夷簡計畫，選一時名臣報使契丹、經略西夏，二邊以寧。

translations.literal: The court relied heavily on Yijian's planning; he selected renowned ministers of the day as envoys in reply to the Khitan and to direct operations against Western Xia, and both frontiers were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The court relied heavily on Yijian's plans, appointing leading ministers as envoys to the Khitan and as frontier commissioners against Western Xia until both borders were quiet again.

sentences.zh: 然建募萬勝軍，雜市井小人，浮脆不任戰鬥。

translations.literal: Yet he established and recruited the Wansheng Army, mixed with market riffraff—unstable and unfit for combat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he also created the Wansheng Army, filled with market-town riffraff—men too soft and undisciplined to fight.

sentences.zh: 用宗室補環衛官，驟增奉賜，又加遺契丹歲繒金二十萬，當時不深計之，其後費大而不可止。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen were used to fill palace guard posts, suddenly increasing stipends and gifts; he also added two hundred thousand in annual silk tribute to the Khitan. At the time this was not examined deeply; afterward the expense grew great and could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He filled palace guard posts with imperial clansmen, sharply increasing stipends, and added two hundred thousand in annual silk tribute to the Khitan. The court did not weigh the long-term cost; later the burden grew and could not be undone.

sentences.zh: 郭后廢，孔道輔等伏閤進諫，而夷簡謂伏閤非太平事，且逐道輔。

translations.literal: When Empress Guo was deposed, Kong Daofu and others prostrated themselves in the gate corridor to remonstrate, but Yijian said that such corridor petitions were no mark of an age at peace and also drove out Daofu.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Guo was deposed, Kong Daofu and others lay across the gate corridor to remonstrate, but Yijian called such protests unbecoming of a peaceful age and had Daofu exiled.

sentences.zh: 其後范仲淹屢言事，獻《百官圖》論遷除之敝，夷簡指為狂肆，斥於外。

translations.literal: Afterwards Fan Zhongyan repeatedly spoke on affairs of state and submitted the "Chart of the Hundred Officials" criticizing abuses in promotions and appointments; Yijian denounced him as reckless and insolent and dismissed him to the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fan Zhongyan repeatedly remonstrated and submitted his "Chart of the Hundred Officials" on abuses in appointments; Yijian branded him arrogant and reckless and sent him away from court.

sentences.zh: 時論以此少之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion therefore thought somewhat less of him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion thought less of him for this.

sentences.zh: 夷簡當國柄最久，雖數為言者所詆，帝眷倚不衰。

translations.literal: Yijian held the reins of state longest; though remonstrators slandered him many times, the Emperor's favor and reliance on him never waned.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian held power longer than anyone, and though critics attacked him repeatedly, the emperor's trust never faded.

sentences.zh: 然所斥士，旋復收用，亦不終廢。

translations.literal: Yet the men he dismissed were soon taken back into service again and were not permanently cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those he dismissed were usually brought back into service and were not permanently ruined.

sentences.zh: 其於天下事，屈伸舒卷，動有操術。

translations.literal: In affairs of the realm he bent and straightened, relaxed and tightened, always with deliberate artifice.
translations.idiomatic: In state affairs he knew when to press and when to yield, and always acted by design.

sentences.zh: 後配食仁宗廟，為世名相。

translations.literal: Later he was granted a place in sacrificial rites at Emperor Renzong's temple, becoming a renowned chief minister of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enshrined in sacrifice at Emperor Renzong's temple and came to be regarded as one of the great ministers of the age.

sentences.zh: 始，王旦奇夷簡，謂王曾曰：「君其善交之。」

translations.literal: At the beginning, Wang Dan regarded Yijian as extraordinary and said to Wang Zeng: "You should make friends with him."
translations.idiomatic: Early on Wang Dan saw something exceptional in Yijian and told Wang Zeng, "You would do well to befriend him."

sentences.zh: 卒與曾並相。

translations.literal: In the end he served as chief minister alongside Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he served as chief minister alongside Wang Zeng.

sentences.zh: 後曾家請御篆墓碑，帝因慘然思夷簡，書「懷忠之碑」四字以賜之。

translations.literal: Later when the Wang Zeng family requested an imperial autograph for a tomb stele, the Emperor, saddened as he thought of Yijian, wrote the four characters "Stele of Cherished Loyalty" and bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Zeng's family asked for an imperial inscription for his tomb stele, the emperor, thinking mournfully of Yijian, wrote the four characters "Stele of Cherished Loyalty" and bestowed them.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left collected writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 子：公綽、公弼、公著、公孺。

translations.literal: His sons: Gongchuo, Gongbi, Gongzhuo, and Gongru.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Gongchuo, Gongbi, Gongzhuo, and Gongru.

sentences.zh: 公著自有傳。

translations.literal: Gongzhuo has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhuo has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 子 公綽

translations.literal: Son Gongchuo
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongchuo

sentences.zh: 公綽，字仲裕，蔭補將作監丞、知陳留縣。

translations.literal: Gongchuo, styled Zhongyu, entered office by yin privilege as Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and magistrate of Chenliu County.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo, styled Zhongyu, entered office through yin privilege as assistant director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and magistrate of Chenliu County.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，為館閣對讀。

translations.literal: During the Tiansheng era he served as collation reader in the palace library institutes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era he served as a collation reader in the palace library institutes.

sentences.zh: 召試，直集賢院，辭，改校理，遷太子中允。

translations.literal: Summoned for examination, he was made a direct access scholar in the Hall of Assembled Worthies; he declined and was changed to collator, then promoted to palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for examination, he was made a direct scholar in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, declined the post, became a collator instead, and was promoted to palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 夷簡罷相，復為直集賢院、同管勾國子監，出知鄭州。

translations.literal: When Yijian left the chief ministership, Gongchuo again became a direct scholar in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and concurrent overseer of the Directorate of Education, then went out as prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yijian left office, Gongchuo again became a direct scholar in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and concurrent overseer of the Directorate of Education, then was posted as prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗問民疾苦，父老曰：「官籍民產，第賦役重輕，至不敢多畜牛，田疇久蕪穢。」

translations.literal: Once he inquired into the people's hardships; the village elders said: "The government registers household property and grades the people for tax and corvée by light and heavy burdens, so that people dare not keep many oxen; fields lie long untilled and overgrown."
translations.idiomatic: Once he asked the people about their hardships, and the elders replied, "Because the government registers household property and grades families for tax and corvée, people dare not keep many oxen, and fields lie long untilled and overgrown."

sentences.zh: 公綽為奏之，自是牛不入籍。

translations.literal: Gongchuo memorialized this, and from that time oxen were no longer entered in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo memorialized the problem, and from then on oxen were no longer entered in household registers.

sentences.zh: 還判吏部南曹，累遷太常博士、同判太常寺。

translations.literal: On returning he served as supervisor of the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, and through successive promotions became erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrent vice-director of that court.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he supervised the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, then rose to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrent vice-director of that court.

sentences.zh: 請復太醫局，及請設令、丞、府史如天官醫師。

translations.literal: He requested restoration of the Medical Service and requested establishment of a director, assistant director, and clerks modeled on the physicians of the Heavenly Office.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the Medical Service be restored and that it be given a director, deputy, and clerks modeled on the physician offices of old.

sentences.zh: 鈞容直假太常旌纛、羽籥，為優人戲，公綽執不可，遂罷之。

translations.literal: The Junrong Guard borrowed imperial banners, flags, and feathered flutes from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to perform as actors for sport; Gongchuo firmly refused and had the practice abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Junrong Guard had been borrowing ritual banners and feathered pipes from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for entertainers to use in comic performances. Gongchuo objected firmly, and the practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He inspected criminal cases in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with inspecting criminal cases in the capital.

sentences.zh: 虎翼卒劉慶告變，下吏案驗，乃慶始謀，眾不從，慶反誣眾以邀賞。

translations.literal: A Tiger-Wing guardsman named Liu Qing reported a mutiny. When officials investigated, it turned out Qing had plotted first, the others had refused to join, and Qing then falsely accused them to claim a reward.
translations.idiomatic: A Tiger-Wing guardsman named Liu Qing reported a mutiny. Investigation showed Qing had plotted it himself, others had refused to follow, and he then falsely accused them to claim a reward.

sentences.zh: 因言：「京師衛兵百萬，不痛懲之，則眾心搖。」

translations.literal: He therefore said: "The capital guards number in the hundreds of thousands; if this is not punished severely, morale will be shaken."
translations.idiomatic: He argued, "There are a hundred thousand capital guards. Unless this is punished severely, morale will waver."

sentences.zh: 遂斬慶以徇。

translations.literal: Qing was then beheaded as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was then beheaded to warn the rest.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書工部員外郎，為史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat and made historiographer of the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Works and made a historiographer in the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 時夷簡雖謝事，猶領國史，公綽辭修撰。

translations.literal: At the time, though Yijian had retired from office he still headed the National History; Gongchuo declined the historiographer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yijian had retired, he still headed the national history, and Gongchuo declined the historiographer post.

sentences.zh: 夷簡薨，還兵部員外郎，復為修撰。

translations.literal: When Yijian died, Gongchuo returned as Vice Director of the Ministry of War and again became historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: After Yijian's death he returned as vice director in the Ministry of War and again served as historiographer.

sentences.zh: 服除，復同判太常寺兼提舉修祭器。

translations.literal: When his mourning period ended, he again served as concurrent vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and commissioner for repairing ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he again served as vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and commissioner for repairing ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 公綽以郊廟祭器未完，制度多違禮，請悉更造。

translations.literal: Gongchuo held that suburban and temple ritual vessels were incomplete and that regulations often violated ritual propriety, and requested that all be remade.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo argued that suburban and temple ritual vessels were incomplete and that current practice often violated ritual propriety, and he asked that everything be remade.

sentences.zh: 故事，薦新諸物，禮官議定乃薦，或後時陳敗。

translations.literal: By precedent, for offerings of seasonal fresh produce, ritual officials had to decide what to offer before offering it, and items were sometimes presented late or spoiled.
translations.idiomatic: Under established practice, offerings of seasonal fresh produce had to be settled by ritual officials before presentation, and items were often offered late or past their prime.

sentences.zh: 公綽採《月令》諸書，以四時新物及所當薦者，配合為圖。

translations.literal: Gongchuo drew on the Monthly Ordinances and similar books to match seasonal fresh items with what should be offered and arranged them in charts.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on the Monthly Ordinances and similar texts, Gongchuo matched seasonal produce with the proper offerings and laid them out in charts.

sentences.zh: 又以歲大、中、小祠凡六十一，禘祫二，祼獻興俯，玉帛尊彝，菁茆醓醢，鐘石歌奏，集為《郊祀總儀》上之。

translations.literal: He also compiled the year's major, intermediate, and minor sacrifices—sixty-one in all—plus the di and xia rites, libation pouring and bowing, jade silks and ritual vessels, thatch and condiments, bells stones and choral accompaniment, gathering them into General Rites for Suburban Sacrifice and submitting it.
translations.idiomatic: He also gathered the year's major, intermediate, and minor sacrifices—sixty-one in all—as well as the di and xia rites, with their libations, bowings, jades, silks, vessels, condiments, bells, stones, and choral parts, and submitted them as General Rites for Suburban Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又言：「古者，天地、宗廟、日月、五方、百神之祀，咸有尊罍，五齊三酒，分實其中，加明水、明酒，以達陰陽之氣。

translations.literal: He also said: "In antiquity, sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, sun and moon, the five directions, and the hundred spirits all had ritual goblets; the five prepared wines and three sacrificial wines were apportioned among them, with clear water and clear wine added to convey the qi of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued, "In antiquity sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, sun and moon, the five directions, and the hundred spirits each had ritual goblets, with the five prepared wines and three sacrificial wines apportioned among them and clear water and clear wine added to convey the forces of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 今有司徒設尊罍，而酌用一尊，非禮神之意。

translations.literal: Now the Minister of Education sets out ritual goblets, yet only one is used in libation—this is not the intent of honoring the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Today the minister of education sets out ritual goblets but uses only one in libation. That does not honor the spirits as ritual requires.

sentences.zh: 宜按《周禮》實齊酒，取火於日，取水於月，因天地之潔氣。」

translations.literal: It would be fitting to follow the Rites of Zhou, filling the prepared wines, taking fire from the sun and water from the moon, thereby using the pure qi of Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: We should follow the Rites of Zhou, fill the prepared wines, take fire from the sun and water from the moon, and thereby draw on the pure powers of Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: 又言：「祖宗配郊，當正位，今側鄉之，非所以示尊嚴也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "When the imperial ancestors accompany the suburban sacrifice, they should occupy the central position; now they are placed to one side facing inward—this does not show the dignity due them."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued, "When the imperial ancestors accompany the suburban sacrifice, they should take the central place. Placing them off to one side does not show the dignity due them."

sentences.zh: 初，諡諸后，皆繫祖宗諡，而真宗五后獨曰「莊」。

translations.literal: At first, when posthumous titles were given to empresses, each was linked to the posthumous title of the emperor; yet of Emperor Zhenzong's five consorts, only one was given "Zhuang."
translations.idiomatic: At first posthumous titles for empresses were linked to the emperor's posthumous title, yet among Emperor Zhenzong's five consorts only one was given the character Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 公綽曰：「婦人從夫之諡，真宗諡章聖，而后曰『莊』，非禮也，願更為『章』。」

translations.literal: Gongchuo said: "A woman's posthumous title follows her husband's. Emperor Zhenzong's posthumous title includes Zhangsheng, yet the consort is called 'Zhuang'—this is unritual. I ask that it be changed to 'Zhang.'"
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo said, "A consort's posthumous title should follow her husband's. Emperor Zhenzong's title includes Zhangsheng, yet she is called Zhuang. That is unritual. I ask that it be changed to Zhang."

sentences.zh: 多施行之。

translations.literal: Many of his proposals were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 歷知制誥、龍圖閣直學士、集賢殿修撰、知永興軍，改樞密直學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: He successively served as drafter of edicts, direct academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs, compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and prefect of Yongxing Army; he was then changed to direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as drafter of edicts, direct academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs, compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and prefect of Yongxing Army, then became direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 安遠砦、古渭州諸羌來獻地，公綽顧其屬曰：「天下之大，豈利區落尺寸地以為廣邪？」

translations.literal: When the Qiang of Anyuan Stockade and ancient Weizhou came to offer land, Gongchuo turned to his staff and said: "The realm is vast—how could one seek to enlarge it by profiting from a few inches of tribal territory?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang of Anyuan Stockade and ancient Weizhou came offering land, Gongchuo turned to his staff and said, "The realm is vast. How could we seek greatness by grabbing a little tribal land?"

sentences.zh: 卻之。

translations.literal: He refused them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the offer.

sentences.zh: 弓箭手馬多闕，公綽諭諸砦戶為三等，凡十丁為社，至秋成，募出金帛市馬，馬少，則先後給之。

translations.literal: Archers and crossbowmen lacked many horses; Gongchuo instructed stockade households to be divided into three grades, with every ten men forming a community; at autumn harvest they would contribute gold and silk to buy horses, and when horses were few they would be allotted in turn according to priority.
translations.idiomatic: Archers and crossbowmen lacked horses. Gongchuo organized stockade households into three grades, with every ten able-bodied men forming a community. At harvest they contributed money and silk to buy horses, allotting them in order when supplies were limited.

sentences.zh: 祀明堂，遷刑部郎中，召為龍圖閣學士、權知開封府。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was sacrificed to, he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Justice and summoned as academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Bright Hall sacrifice he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Justice and summoned to serve as academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，願罷府事，進翰林侍讀學士、知審刑院兼判太常寺。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he asked to be relieved of prefectural duties and was promoted to Hanlin Attendant Reader, put in charge of the Court for Review of Punishments, and made concurrent vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he asked to leave the prefecture and was made Hanlin attendant reader, put in charge of the Court for Review of Punishments, and given concurrent duty in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 初，公綽在開封府，宰相龐籍外屬道士趙清貺受賂，杖脊道死。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Gongchuo was at the Kaifeng prefecture, the Taoist Zhao Qingchang—an outside relation of Chief Councillor Pang Ji—accepted bribes and died on the road after being beaten with the bamboo rod on the back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Gongchuo was at Kaifeng, the Taoist Zhao Qingchang, a relative by marriage of Chief Councillor Pang Ji, took bribes and died on the road after a back beating.

sentences.zh: 至是，御史以為公綽受籍旨，杖殺清貺以滅口，左遷龍圖閣學士、知徐州。

translations.literal: At this point the censors held that Gongchuo had acted on Ji's instruction, beating Qingchang to death to silence him, and he was demoted to academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The censors then charged that Gongchuo had acted on Ji's orders and beaten Qingchang to death to silence him. He was demoted to academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and sent to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 方杖清貺時，實非公綽所臨。

translations.literal: When Qingchang was beaten, Gongchuo had in fact not been in charge.
translations.idiomatic: In fact Gongchuo had not been present when Qingchang was beaten.

sentences.zh: 頃之，公綽亦自辨，復侍讀學士，徙河陽，留侍經筵。

translations.literal: Before long Gongchuo also defended himself; he was restored as attendant reader, transferred to Heyang, and retained to attend the emperor's lecture sessions.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gongchuo defended himself, was restored as attendant reader, transferred to Heyang, and kept on to attend the emperor's lectures.

sentences.zh: 時久不雨，帝顧問：「何以致雨？」

translations.literal: When rain had long failed to fall, the Emperor turned and asked: "What will bring rain?"
translations.idiomatic: During a long drought the emperor asked, "What will bring rain?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「獄久不決，即有冤者，故多旱。」

translations.literal: He replied: "When cases in prison go long undecided there are surely wronged persons; hence much drought."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "When cases go long undecided, innocent people remain wronged. That is why droughts are common."

sentences.zh: 帝親慮囚，已而大雨。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally reviewed prisoners, and soon after heavy rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally reviewed prisoners, and soon afterward heavy rain fell.

sentences.zh: 遷右司郎中，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Right Bureau but before taking office he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the right bureau but died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 贈左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Left Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left remonstrance grandee.

sentences.zh: 公綽通敏有才，父執政時，多涉干請，喜名好進者趨之。

translations.literal: Gongchuo was quick and talented; while his father held power he was often involved in personal solicitations, and those who loved reputation and sought advancement flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo was quick-witted and capable. While his father held power he was often entangled in personal solicitations, and those hungry for fame and advancement flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗漏泄除拜以市恩，時人比之竇申。

translations.literal: He once leaked appointment orders to curry favor; people of the time compared him to Dou Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He once leaked appointment news to buy favor, and contemporaries compared him to Dou Shen.

sentences.zh: 子 公弼

translations.literal: Son Gongbi
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongbi

sentences.zh: 公弼，字寶臣。

translations.literal: Gongbi, styled Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi, styled Baochen.

sentences.zh: 賜進士出身，積遷直史館、河北轉運使。

translations.literal: Granted jinshi initial appointment, he rose through successive posts to direct access in the Historiography Office and transport commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Granted jinshi initial appointment, he rose through successive posts to direct access in the Historiography Office and transport commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 自寶元、慶歷以來，宿師備邊。

translations.literal: From the Baoyuan and Qingli eras onward, standing armies had long guarded the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Baoyuan and Qingli eras the court had kept standing armies on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 既西北撤警，而將屯如故，民疲饋餉。

translations.literal: After the northwestern alarm was lifted, military colonies remained as before, and the people were exhausted providing supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the northwestern threat eased, garrisons stayed in place and the people were worn out supplying them.

sentences.zh: 公弼始通御河，漕粟實塞下，冶鐵以助經費；

translations.literal: Gongbi first opened the Imperial Canal, transported grain to fill the border forts, and smelted iron to supplement expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi opened the Imperial Canal, shipped grain to stock the border forts, and smelted iron to help cover costs.

sentences.zh: 移近邊屯兵就食京東；

translations.literal: He moved border garrison troops nearby to be fed in eastern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He moved frontier garrisons nearer so they could be fed from eastern Jing.

sentences.zh: 增城卒，給板築；

translations.literal: He increased city garrison troops and supplied them for wall building.
translations.idiomatic: He added city garrison troops and supplied them for rampart work.

sentences.zh: 蠲冗賦及民逋數百萬。

translations.literal: He remitted redundant levies and arrears owed by the people amounting to several million.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted redundant levies and popular tax arrears totaling several million.

sentences.zh: 夷簡之亡也，仁宗思之，問知公弼名，識於殿柱。

translations.literal: When Yijian died, Emperor Renzong thought of him, asked and learned Gongbi's name, and wrote it on a palace pillar.
translations.idiomatic: After Yijian's death Emperor Renzong missed him, asked after Gongbi's name, and wrote it on a palace pillar.

sentences.zh: 至是，益材其為。

translations.literal: At this point the Emperor valued his talent all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor valued his abilities all the more.

sentences.zh: 擢都轉運使，加龍圖閣直學士、知瀛州，入權開封府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to overall transport commissioner, given the additional title of direct academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and made prefect of Yingzhou, then entered the capital as acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to overall transport commissioner, made direct academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and prefect of Yingzhou, then entered the capital as acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏事退，帝目送之，謂宰相曰：「公弼甚似其父。」

translations.literal: Once after he had reported on business and withdrawn, the Emperor watched him go and said to the chief ministers: "Gongbi greatly resembles his father."
translations.idiomatic: Once, after he reported on business and withdrew, the emperor watched him go and told the chief ministers, "Gongbi greatly resembles his father."

sentences.zh: 改同群牧使，以樞密直學士知渭、延二州，徙成都府。

translations.literal: He was changed to Concurrent Commissioner of the Horse Pasturage Office, served as direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs administering Wei and Yan prefectures, and was transferred to Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became concurrent commissioner of the Horse Pasturage Office, served as direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs over Wei and Yan prefectures, and was transferred to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 其治尚寬，人疑少威斷。

translations.literal: His governance tended toward leniency, and people suspected he lacked firm decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: His rule tended toward leniency, and some thought him short on forceful judgment.

sentences.zh: 營卒犯法當杖，捍不受，曰：「寧以劍死。」

translations.literal: A garrison soldier guilty of an offense deserving the rod resisted and would not submit, saying: "I would rather die by the sword."
translations.idiomatic: A garrison soldier due for the rod resisted and refused it, saying, "I would rather die by the sword."

sentences.zh: 公弼曰：「杖者國法，劍汝自請。」

translations.literal: Gongbi said: "The rod is the law of the state; the sword is your own request."
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi said, "The rod is the law of the land. If you want the sword, that is your choice."

sentences.zh: 杖而後斬之，軍府肅然。

translations.literal: He was beaten with the rod and then beheaded; the army headquarters became thoroughly orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten and then beheaded, and the garrison command became thoroughly orderly.

sentences.zh: 英宗罷三司使蔡襄，召公弼代之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong dismissed Three Departments Commissioner Cai Xiang and summoned Gongbi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong dismissed Three Departments commissioner Cai Xiang and summoned Gongbi to replace him.

sentences.zh: 初，公弼在群牧時，帝居藩，得賜馬頗劣，欲易不可。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gongbi was at the Horse Pasturage Office, while the Emperor was still in his princely residence he received a gift horse that was rather poor and wished to exchange it but was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Gongbi was at the Horse Pasturage Office, the emperor—then still a prince—received a gift horse of poor quality and wanted to exchange it but was refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝謂曰：「卿曩歲不與朕馬，是時固已知卿矣。

translations.literal: At this point the Emperor said to him: "In those years you would not give me a horse; even then I already knew you.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor told him, "Years ago you would not swap my horse for a better one. Even then I knew what sort of man you were.

sentences.zh: 蔡襄主計，訴訟不時決，故多留事。

translations.literal: Cai Xiang had managed accounts; lawsuits were not decided in timely fashion, so many matters were left pending.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang had run the accounts, lawsuits were not decided promptly, and much business had been left undone.

sentences.zh: 卿繼其後，將何以處之？」

translations.literal: You follow in his place; how will you handle it?"
translations.idiomatic: You are taking his place. How do you plan to handle things?"

sentences.zh: 公弼頓首謝，對曰：「襄勤於事，未嘗有曠失，恐言之者妄耳。」

translations.literal: Gongbi bowed his head in thanks and replied: "Xiang was diligent in affairs and never had neglect or lapse; I fear the accusers speak falsely."
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi kowtowed in thanks and answered, "Xiang was diligent in his duties and never neglected them. I fear his accusers spoke falsely."

sentences.zh: 帝以為長者。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered him a man of mature restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took him for a man of mature judgment.

sentences.zh: 拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時言事者數與大臣異議去，公弼諫曰：「諫官、御史，為陛下耳目，執政為股肱。

translations.literal: At the time remonstrators repeatedly departed over disagreements with chief ministers. Gongbi remonstrated: "Remonstrance officials and censors serve as Your Majesty's eyes and ears; the chief ministers are your arms and legs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time remonstrators often left office after clashing with chief ministers. Gongbi admonished, "Remonstrance officials and censors are Your Majesty's eyes and ears, and the chief ministers are your arms and legs.

sentences.zh: 股肱耳目，必相為用，然後身安而元首尊。

translations.literal: Arms, legs, eyes, and ears must be used together—only then is the body secure and the sovereign's head honored.
translations.idiomatic: Arms, legs, eyes, and ears must work together before the body is secure and the ruler's dignity upheld.

sentences.zh: 宜考言觀事，視其所以而進退之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should examine words and observe deeds, see what motivates them, and promote or dismiss accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should weigh their words and deeds, see what truly drives them, and promote or dismiss accordingly."

sentences.zh: 彗出營室，帝憂之，同列請飭邊備。

translations.literal: A comet appeared in the Encampment; the Emperor was troubled. His colleagues requested strengthening border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared in the Encampment, the emperor grew anxious and his colleagues urged tightening border defenses.

sentences.zh: 公弼曰：「彗非小變，陛下宜側身修德，以應天戒，臣恐患不在邊也。」

translations.literal: Gongbi said: "A comet is no minor omen. Your Majesty should examine yourself and cultivate virtue to respond to Heaven's warning. I fear the trouble lies not on the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi said, "A comet is no minor portent. Your Majesty should examine his conduct and cultivate virtue in answer to Heaven's warning. I fear the danger lies not on the frontier."

sentences.zh: 神宗立，司馬光劾內侍高居簡，帝未決。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne, Sima Guang impeached the inner attendant Gao Jujian; the Emperor had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Sima Guang impeached the eunuch Gao Jujian, and the emperor had not yet decided the case.

sentences.zh: 公弼曰：「光與居簡，勢不兩立。

translations.literal: Gongbi said: "Guang and Jujian cannot both stand.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi said, "Guang and Jujian cannot both remain in power.

sentences.zh: 居簡，內臣耳，而光中執法，願陛下擇其重者。」

translations.literal: Jujian is only an inner servant, whereas Guang holds the center of law enforcement. I hope Your Majesty will choose the weightier one."
translations.idiomatic: Jujian is only an inner attendant, while Guang holds central authority over the law. Your Majesty should choose the one who matters more."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然則當奈何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Then what should be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Then what should be done?"

sentences.zh: 公弼曰：「遷居簡一官，而解其近職，光當無爭。」

translations.literal: Gongbi said: "Transfer Jujian one rank and remove him from close duties; Guang should then make no further dispute."
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi said, "Transfer Jujian to another post and remove him from his close duties. Guang should then let the matter rest."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 進樞密使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 議者欲倂環慶、鄜延為一路，公弼曰：「自白草西抵定遠，中間相去千里，若合為一路，猝有緩急，將何以應？」

translations.literal: Some proposed merging Huanqing and Yan-Yan circuits into one route. Gongbi said: "From Baicao west to Dingyuan the distance in between is a thousand li. If combined into one route, in a sudden emergency how would one respond?"
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed merging the Huanqing and Yan-Yan circuits into one command. Gongbi objected, "From Baicao west to Dingyuan the distance spans a thousand li. If merged into one route, how could we respond to a sudden emergency?"

sentences.zh: 又欲下邊臣使議之，公弼曰：「廟堂之上不處決，而諉邊吏，可乎？」

translations.literal: Some also wanted to refer the matter to border officials for discussion. Gongbi said: "If the court above does not decide but shifts responsibility to frontier clerks, is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Others wanted to leave the decision to frontier officials. Gongbi said, "Can it be right for the court not to decide and push the matter down to border officers?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 王安石知政事，嗛公弼不附己，白用其弟公著為御史中丞以逼之。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi directed state affairs, he resented that Gongbi did not align with him and proposed using Gongbi's younger brother Gongzhuo as Censor-in-Chief to pressure him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi ran the government, he resented Gongbi's independence and proposed making Gongbi's younger brother Gongzhuo censor-in-chief to pressure him.

sentences.zh: 公弼不自安，立上章避位，不許。

translations.literal: Gongbi felt unsafe and immediately submitted a memorial to resign his post; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Gongbi promptly submitted a memorial to resign, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 陳升之建議，衛兵年四十以上，稍不中程者，減其牢廩，徙之淮南。

translations.literal: Chen Shengzhi proposed that capital guards over forty who failed fitness standards slightly should have their rations reduced and be transferred to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengzhi proposed that capital guards over forty who fell slightly short of fitness standards should have their rations cut and be transferred to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 公弼以為非人情，帝曰：「是當退為剩員者，今故為優假，何所害？」

translations.literal: Gongbi held this contrary to human feeling. The Emperor said: "These are men who ought to be retired as surplus personnel; now we are deliberately showing them leniency—what harm is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi thought this violated basic human feeling. The emperor said, "These men ought to be retired as surplus personnel. We are deliberately treating them leniently. What harm could that do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣不敢生事邀名，正恐誤國耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant dares not stir up trouble to win a name; I truly fear misleading the state.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I dare not stir up trouble for reputation's sake. I truly fear misleading the state.

sentences.zh: 既使去本土，又削其廩，儻二十萬眾皆反側，為之奈何？」

translations.literal: Having sent them far from their native place and also cut their rations, if two hundred thousand men all grow restive, what will be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: If we send them away from home and cut their rations, what if two hundred thousand men all grow restless? What then?"

sentences.zh: 韓絳議復肉刑，公弼力陳不可，帝皆為之止。

translations.literal: Han Jiang proposed restoring mutilation punishments; Gongbi forcefully argued this was impossible, and in both cases the Emperor stopped the proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang proposed restoring mutilation punishments and Gongbi forcefully objected; the emperor halted both proposals.

sentences.zh: 安石立新法，公弼數言宜務安靜，又將疏論之。

translations.literal: When Anshi established new laws, Gongbi repeatedly said affairs should be kept calm and was about to submit a memorial criticizing them.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi introduced his new laws, Gongbi repeatedly argued for calm and was preparing a memorial against them.

sentences.zh: 從孫嘉問竊其稿示安石，安石先白之，帝不樂，遂罷為觀文殿學士、知太原府。

translations.literal: His nephew Sun Jiawen stole the draft and showed it to Anshi. Anshi reported first; the Emperor was displeased, and Gongbi was dismissed to academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Sun Jiawen stole the draft and showed it to Anshi, who reported it first. The emperor was displeased and dismissed Gongbi to academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 韓絳宣撫秦、晉，將取囉兀城，令河東發兵二萬，趣神堂新路。

translations.literal: Han Jiang as pacification commissioner for Qin and Jin planned to take Luowu city and ordered Hedong to raise twenty thousand troops to hurry by the Shen Tang new route.
