translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang, pacification commissioner for Qin and Jin, planned to take Luowu city and ordered Hedong to dispatch twenty thousand troops along the Shen Tang new route.

sentences.zh: 公弼曰：「虜必設伏以待我。

translations.literal: Gongbi said: "The enemy will surely set an ambush to await us.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi warned, "The enemy will surely lay an ambush along that route.

sentences.zh: 永和關雖回遠，可安行無患。」

translations.literal: The Yonghe Pass route, though circuitous and long, can be traveled safely without danger."
translations.idiomatic: The Yonghe Pass route is longer, but we can travel it safely."

sentences.zh: 乃由永和。

translations.literal: They therefore took the Yonghe route.
translations.idiomatic: They marched by way of Yonghe instead.

sentences.zh: 既而新路援兵果遇伏，詔褒之。

translations.literal: Before long troops on the new route indeed met an ambush; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward troops on the new route were indeed ambushed, and an edict praised Gongbi's judgment.

sentences.zh: 麟州無井，唯沙泉在城外，欲拓城包之，而土善陷，夏人每至圍城，人皆憂渴死。

translations.literal: Linzhou had no wells; only a sandy spring lay outside the walls. They wished to expand the city to encompass it, but the soil readily caved in. Whenever the Tangut came and besieged the city, people feared dying of thirst.
translations.idiomatic: Linzhou had no wells and relied on a sandy spring outside the walls. They wanted to expand the city to include it, but the soil kept collapsing. Whenever the Tangut besieged the city, people feared dying of thirst.

sentences.zh: 公弼用其僚鄧子喬計，仿古拔軸法，去其沙，實以末炭，墳土於其上，板築立，遂包泉於中。

translations.literal: Gongbi used the plan of his staff officer Deng Ziqiao, following the ancient stake-extraction method: removing the sand, filling with charcoal powder, heaping earth above, building ramparts on it, and thus enclosing the spring within.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi adopted a plan from his staff officer Deng Ziqiao, following an ancient method of driving piles: they removed the sand, filled the space with charcoal powder, piled earth on top, and built ramparts so the spring was enclosed within the walls.

sentences.zh: 自是城堅不陷，而州得以守。

translations.literal: From then the walls stood firm without collapsing, and the prefecture could be held.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the walls held firm and the prefecture could be defended.

sentences.zh: 子 公孺

translations.literal: Son Gongru
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongru

sentences.zh: 公孺，字稚卿。

translations.literal: Gongru, styled Zhiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Gongru, styled Zhiqing.

sentences.zh: 任為奉禮郎，賜進士出身，判吏部南曹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Ceremonial Gentleman, granted jinshi initial appointment, and served as supervisor of the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed ceremonial gentleman, granted jinshi initial appointment, and assigned to the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 占對詳敏，仁宗以為可用。

translations.literal: His extemporaneous replies were detailed and quick; Emperor Renzong considered him usable.
translations.idiomatic: His impromptu replies were detailed and sharp, and Emperor Renzong judged him capable.

sentences.zh: 知澤、潁、廬、常四州，提點福建、河北路刑獄，入為開封府推官。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Ze, Ying, Lu, and Chang prefectures, as judicial intendant of Fujian and Hebei circuits, and entered the capital as investigating official of the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Ze, Ying, Lu, and Chang, as judicial intendant on the Fujian and Hebei circuits, and entered the capital as an investigating official in Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 民鬻薪為盜所奪，逐之遭傷，尹包拯命笞盜。

translations.literal: A man selling firewood had it seized by a thief; pursuing the thief he was injured; Prefect Bao Zheng ordered the thief beaten with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: A man selling firewood had his load stolen; when he gave chase he was injured. Prefect Bao Zheng ordered the thief flogged.

sentences.zh: 公孺曰：「盜而傷主，法不止笞。」

translations.literal: Gongru said: "A thief who injures the owner—the law does not stop at beating with the rod."
translations.idiomatic: Gongru objected, "A thief who injures the owner deserves more than a beating."

sentences.zh: 執不從，拯善其守。

translations.literal: He persisted in his objection; Bao did not agree, but admired his firm adherence to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Gongru held firm to his view; Bao did not yield, but admired his adherence to the law.

sentences.zh: 及使三司，而公孺為判官，事皆咨決之。

translations.literal: When Bao was sent to the Three Departments, with Gongru as vice-director, all affairs were referred to him for decision.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao headed the Three Departments with Gongru as his deputy, he consulted Gongru on every matter.

sentences.zh: 判都水監，未幾，改陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as vice-director of the Directorate of Waterways; before long he was changed to transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-director of the Directorate of Waterways and soon became transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 神宗得綏州，遣使議守棄之便，久未決。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took Suizhou, he sent envoys to discuss the advisability of holding or abandoning it, but long could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shenzong captured Suizhou, he sent envoys to debate whether to hold or abandon it, but the court could not decide for a long time.

sentences.zh: 命公孺往，與郭逵議合，遂存綏州。

translations.literal: Gongru was ordered to go; his opinion agreed with Guo Kui's, and Suizhou was therefore retained.
translations.idiomatic: Gongru was sent to investigate; he agreed with Guo Kui, and Suizhou was kept.

sentences.zh: 常平法行，公孺請以青苗、免役歸提刑司。

translations.literal: When the Ever-Normal Granary law was implemented, Gongru requested that Green Sprouts and Labor Exemption be placed under the judicial intendant offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ever-Normal Granary system took effect, Gongru asked that Green Sprouts loans and the labor-exemption tax be placed under the judicial intendant offices.

sentences.zh: 徙知渭州，再徙鄆州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Weizhou, then again transferred to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Weizhou and then to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐失入死刑，責知蔡州。

translations.literal: For wrongly imposing the death penalty he was demoted to prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For wrongly imposing the death penalty he was demoted and sent to Caizhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，帝召公孺，慰之曰：「長安謀帥，無以易卿。」

translations.literal: Early in the Yuanfeng era the Emperor summoned Gongru and consoled him: "In seeking a commander for Chang'an, none can replace you."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanfeng era the emperor summoned Gongru and reassured him, "In choosing a commander for Chang'an, no one can replace you."

sentences.zh: 命知永興軍。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as prefect of Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 徙河陽，洛口兵千人，以久役思歸，奮斧鍤排關，不得入，西走河橋，觀聽洶洶。

translations.literal: Transferred to Heyang, a thousand Luokou troops, weary of long service and longing to return, seized axes and spades and broke through the gate but could not enter; they fled west to the river bridge, and onlookers grew turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: After he was transferred to Heyang, a thousand Luokou troops, weary from long service and longing to go home, took up axes and spades and tried to break through the gate. Blocked, they fled west toward the river bridge as the crowd grew restive.

sentences.zh: 諸將請出兵掩擊，公孺曰：「此皆亡命，急之，變且生。」

translations.literal: The generals asked to send troops for a surprise attack. Gongru said: "These are all desperate men; if pressed hard, a mutiny will arise."
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged a surprise attack. Gongru said, "These are desperate men. Press them hard and a revolt will follow."

sentences.zh: 即乘馬東去，遣牙兵數人迎諭之曰：「汝輩誠勞苦，然豈得擅還？

translations.literal: He immediately rode east and sent several guard soldiers to meet and instruct them: "You indeed suffer hardship, but how can you return without permission?
translations.idiomatic: He rode east himself and sent several guards ahead to tell them, "You have indeed suffered, but how can you leave without permission?

sentences.zh: 一度橋，則罪不赦矣！

translations.literal: Once you cross the bridge, the offense will not be pardoned!
translations.idiomatic: Once you cross that bridge, your crime will be beyond pardon!

sentences.zh: 太守在此，願自首者止道左。」

translations.literal: The prefect is here; those who wish to surrender should stop on the left of the road."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect is here. Those willing to surrender should stop on the left side of the road."

sentences.zh: 皆佇立以俟。

translations.literal: They all stood in place waiting.
translations.idiomatic: They all halted and waited.

sentences.zh: 公孺索倡首者，黥一人，餘復送役所。

translations.literal: Gongru sought the ringleaders, tattooed one man, and sent the rest back to their labor posts.
translations.idiomatic: Gongru identified the ringleaders, tattooed one man, and sent the rest back to duty.

sentences.zh: 語其校曰：「若復偃蹇者，斬而後報。」

translations.literal: He told their commander: "If any again show insubordination, behead first and report afterward."
translations.idiomatic: He told their commander, "If anyone again shows defiance, execute first and report afterward."

sentences.zh: 眾帖息。

translations.literal: The crowd submitted and quieted.
translations.idiomatic: The troops submitted and calmed down.

sentences.zh: 乃自劾專命，詔釋之。

translations.literal: He then impeached himself for acting on his own authority; an edict released him from blame.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a self-accusation for acting on his own authority, and an edict exonerated him.

sentences.zh: 知審官東院，出知秦州。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Eastern Bureau for Review of Officials and went out as prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the eastern bureau for review of officials, then went out to serve as prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 李憲以詔出兵，欲盡駐原、渭，公孺不可，與憲相論奏，坐徙相州，更陳、杭、鄭、瀛四州。

translations.literal: Li Xian was ordered by edict to mobilize troops and wished to concentrate them all at Yuan and Wei; Gongru objected; he and Xian exchanged memorials debating the matter; he was transferred to Xiangzhou for this, and later also served Chen, Hang, Zheng, and Ying prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian was ordered to mobilize and wanted to concentrate all troops at Yuan and Wei. Gongru objected; he and Li Xian exchanged competing memorials, and Gongru was transferred to Xiangzhou and later also served at Chen, Hang, Zheng, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，加龍圖閣直學士，復以為秦州，固辭，改秘書監。

translations.literal: Early in the Yuanyou era he was given the additional title of direct academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and again appointed to Qinzhou; he firmly declined and was changed to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era he was made direct academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and again offered Qinzhou, but he declined firmly and was made director of the Secretariat instead.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部侍郎、知開封府，為政明恕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and prefect of Kaifeng; his governance was clear and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of justice and prefect of Kaifeng, governing with clarity and leniency.

sentences.zh: 幕人遷黼坐設，毀其角，法當徒，公孺請罪，數十人皆以杖免。

translations.literal: A staff member named Qian Fu was seated at a reception and broke the corner of his seat; by law he deserved penal servitude. Gongru pleaded guilty on his behalf, and several dozen men were all released with beating instead.
translations.idiomatic: A staff member named Qian Fu broke the corner of his seat at a reception; by law he deserved penal servitude. Gongru took the blame, and several dozen men were all released with a beating instead.

sentences.zh: 原廟亡珠，繫治典吏久，公孺曰：「主者番代不一，曷嘗以珠數相授受，歲時諱日，宮嬪狎至，奈何顓指吏卒乎？」

translations.literal: When pearls were lost from the original temple, supervising officers were long detained for investigation. Gongru said: "Those in charge changed with each rotation—when were pearls ever counted hand to hand in transfer? On annual taboo days palace women came freely—how can blame fall solely on clerks and guards?"
translations.idiomatic: When pearls went missing from the imperial shrine, the responsible officials were held for a long investigation. Gongru argued, "Those in charge changed with each rotation. Pearls were never counted at each handover. On annual memorial days palace women came and went freely. How can blame fall on clerks alone?"

sentences.zh: 請之，得釋。

translations.literal: He petitioned on their behalf and they were released.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for them and they were released.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部尚書，以病，提舉醴泉觀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue; due to illness he was made commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of revenue, but illness led to his appointment as commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Right Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made right grandee of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 公孺廉儉，與人寡合。

translations.literal: Gongru was frugal and had few close associations with others.
translations.idiomatic: Gongru was frugal and kept to himself.

sentences.zh: 嘗護曹佾喪，得厚餉，辭不受，談者清其節焉。

translations.literal: Once while escorting Cao Yu's funeral he received lavish payment but declined to accept it; commentators praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while overseeing Cao Yu's funeral, he was offered lavish payment but refused it; observers praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 張士遜

translations.literal: Zhang Shixun
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shixun

sentences.zh: 張士遜，字順之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shixun, styled Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shixun, styled Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 祖裕，嘗主陰城鹽院，因家陰城。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu once managed the Yincheng salt depot and therefore made his home in Yincheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had managed the Yincheng salt depot and settled the family there.

sentences.zh: 士遜生百日始啼。

translations.literal: Shixun did not cry until a hundred days after birth.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun did not cry until he was a hundred days old.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，舉進士，調鄖鄉主簿，遷射洪令。

translations.literal: During the Chunhua era he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as registrar of Yunxiang, and was transferred to magistrate of Shehong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era he passed the jinshi examination, served as registrar of Yunxiang, and became magistrate of Shehong.

sentences.zh: 轉運使檄移士遜治郪，民遮馬首不得去，因聽還射洪。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner issued orders transferring Shixun to Qi; the people blocked his horse's path so he could not leave, and he was therefore allowed to return to Shehong.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner ordered Shixun transferred to Qi, but the people blocked his horse and would not let him leave, so he was allowed to remain at Shehong.

sentences.zh: 安撫使至梓州，問屬吏能否，知州張雍曰：「射洪令，第一也。」

translations.literal: When the pacification commissioner reached Zizhou and asked about the ability of subordinate officials, Prefect Zhang Yong said: "The magistrate of Shehong is first."
translations.idiomatic: When the pacification commissioner reached Zizhou and asked about local officials, Prefect Zhang Yong said, "The magistrate of Shehong is the best."

sentences.zh: 改襄陽令，為秘書省著作佐郎、知邵武縣，以寬厚得民。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Xiangyang, made Assistant Compiler of the Secretariat, and prefect of Shaowu County, winning the people through leniency and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Xiangyang, then assistant compiler in the Secretariat and prefect of Shaowu, winning the people with his generous rule.

sentences.zh: 前治射洪，以旱，禱雨白崖山陸使君祠，尋大雨，士遜立廷中，須雨足乃去。

translations.literal: Earlier while governing Shehong, during drought he prayed for rain at the shrine of Lord Lu on White Cliff Mountain; soon heavy rain fell, and Shixun stood in the courtyard until the rain was fully sufficient before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Shehong during a drought, he prayed for rain at the shrine of Lord Lu on White Cliff Mountain. Heavy rain soon fell, and Shixun stood in the courtyard until the downpour was complete before leaving.

sentences.zh: 至是，邵武旱，禱歐陽太守廟，廟去城過一舍，士遜徹蓋，雨沾足始歸。

translations.literal: At this time Shaowu suffered drought; he prayed at the shrine of Administrator Ouyang, which lay more than one stopping-place from the city. Shixun removed his parasol and did not return until the rain had soaked the ground fully.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaowu suffered drought, he prayed at the shrine of Administrator Ouyang more than ten li from the city, removed his parasol, and did not return until the rain had thoroughly soaked the ground.

sentences.zh: 改秘書丞、監折中倉，歷御史臺推直官。

translations.literal: He was changed to Secretary of the Secretariat, supervisor of the Median Granary, and served successively as investigating officer of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He became secretary of the Secretariat, supervisor of the Median Granary, and served as an investigating officer in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士楊億薦為監察御史。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Yang Yi recommended him as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Yang Yi recommended him for appointment as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 貢舉初用糊名法，士遜為諸科巡鋪官，以進士有姻黨，士遜請避去，真宗記名於御屏，自是有親嫌者皆移試，著為令。

translations.literal: When the examination system first used the sealed-name method, Shixun was patrol officer for the various subjects; as a jinshi he had marriage connections, so Shixun asked to withdraw. Emperor Zhenzong wrote his name on the imperial screen; from then on those with personal connections all took separate examinations, which was established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the examinations first used sealed-name papers, Shixun served as patrol officer. Because he had family ties among the jinshi candidates, he asked to recuse himself. Emperor Zhenzong noted his name on the imperial screen, and from then on those with personal conflicts took separate exams—a rule that became permanent law.

sentences.zh: 中書擬人充江南轉運使，再擬輒見卻，帝獨用士遜。

translations.literal: The Secretariat proposed men to fill the Jiangnan transport commissioner post; twice proposals were rejected, and the Emperor used Shixun alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat twice proposed candidates for Jiangnan transport commissioner and both lists were rejected; the emperor appointed Shixun alone.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍御史，徙廣東，又徙河北。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to attendant censor and transferred to Guangdong, then again to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant censor, transferred to Guangdong, and then to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 河侵棣州，詔徙州陽信，議者患糧多，不可遷。

translations.literal: The Yellow River encroached on Dizhou; an edict ordered moving the prefectural seat to Yangxin; debaters feared too much grain and that relocation was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River threatened Dizhou, an edict ordered moving the prefectural seat to Yangxin. Critics worried that the grain supply was too large to move.

sentences.zh: 士遜視瀕河數州方艱食，即計餘以貸貧者，期來歲輸陽信，公私利之。

translations.literal: Shixun saw that several Yellow-River-border prefectures were short of food; he immediately counted surpluses to lend to the poor, planning that next year they would deliver to Yangxin—public and private both benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun saw that several river-border prefectures were short of food. He counted available surpluses and lent to the poor, planning for delivery to Yangxin the following year. Both government and people benefited.

sentences.zh: 仁宗出閣，帝選僚佐，謂宰臣曰：「翊善、記室，府屬也，王皆受拜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong left the inner quarters, the Emperor chose staff assistants and told the chief ministers: "Tutors and recorders are princely household officials; the prince all receives their bows.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong left the inner palace, the emperor chose staff for him and told the chief ministers, "Tutors and recorders are household officials of the prince, and the prince receives their bows.

sentences.zh: 今王尚少，宜以士遜為友，令王答拜。」

translations.literal: Now the prince is still young; Shixun should serve as friend, and the prince should return the bow."
translations.idiomatic: The prince is still young. Shixun should serve as his companion, and the prince should return the bow."

sentences.zh: 於是以戶部郎中直昭文館，為壽春郡王友，改昇王府諮議參軍，遷右諫議大夫兼太子右庶子，改左庶子。

translations.literal: Thereupon, as Director in the Ministry of Revenue with direct access in the Hall of Splendid Culture, he became friend to the Prince of Shouchun; was changed to advisory attache of the Prince of Sheng's establishment; was promoted to Right Remonstrance Grandee and concurrent Right Subsidiary Heir Apparent; and was changed to Left Subsidiary Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made director in the Ministry of Revenue with direct access in the Hall of Splendid Culture and friend to the Prince of Shouchun, then advisory attache in the Prince of Sheng's household, right remonstrance grandee and right subsidiary heir apparent, and finally left subsidiary heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 士遜言：「詣資善堂，升階列拜，而皇太子猶跪受，宜詔皇太子坐受之。」

translations.literal: Shixun said: "When attending the Hall of Cultivating Goodness, one ascends the steps and lines up to bow, yet the crown prince still kneels to receive it. An edict should order the crown prince to receive bows while seated."
translations.idiomatic: Shixun argued, "When we attend the Hall of Cultivating Goodness, we ascend the steps and bow in line, yet the crown prince still kneels to receive us. An edict should allow the crown prince to receive bows while seated."

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 詔士遜等遇太子侍駕出入許陪從。

translations.literal: An edict granted that when Shixun and others met the crown prince attending the imperial carriage on going in and out, they were permitted to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed Shixun and the others to accompany the crown prince when he attended the emperor on formal outings.

sentences.zh: 判史館，知審刑院，以太子賓客、樞密直學士判集賢院。

translations.literal: He directed the Historiography Office, managed the Court for Review of Punishments, and as Guest of the Crown Prince and direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs directed the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the Historiography Office and the Court for Review of Punishments, and as guest of the crown prince and direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs directed the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 既而二府大臣皆領東宮官，遂換太子詹事，擢樞密副使，遷給事中兼詹事，累遷尚書左丞，遂拜禮部尚書、同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: Before long chief ministers of both bureaus all held Eastern Palace posts; he was then exchanged to Grand Steward of the Crown Prince, promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, transferred to Drafting Attendant-in-Ordinary concurrently as Grand Steward, through successive promotions to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and finally appointed Minister of Rites, Co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Grand Academic Scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon chief ministers of both bureaus also held Eastern Palace posts, so he was made grand steward of the crown prince instead, promoted to vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then drafting attendant-in-ordinary and grand steward, and rose through left vice director of the Secretariat to minister of rites, co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and grand academic scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 曹汭獄事起，宦者羅崇勳、江德明方用事，因譖利用。

translations.literal: When the Cao Rui prison case arose, the eunuchs Luo Chongxun and Jiang Deming were just then wielding power, and they took the occasion to slander Cao Liyong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Cao Rui case broke, the eunuchs Luo Chongxun and Jiang Deming, who were then in power, seized the chance to slander Cao Liyong.

sentences.zh: 帝疑之，問執政，眾顧望未有對者。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew suspicious and questioned the chief ministers; everyone looked about, and none answered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and asked the chief ministers. They looked to one another, and no one spoke.

sentences.zh: 士遜徐曰：「此獨不肖子為之，利用大臣，宜不知狀。」

translations.literal: Shixun said slowly: "This was done only by an unworthy son. As a great minister, Liyong surely did not know the circumstances."
translations.idiomatic: Shixun said calmly, "This was the work of an unworthy son alone. As a senior minister, Liyong surely knew nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 太后怒，將罷士遜。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was angry and was about to dismiss Shixun.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was furious and was about to remove Shixun from office.

sentences.zh: 帝以其東宮舊臣，加刑部尚書、知江寧府，解通犀帶賜之。

translations.literal: Because he was an old Eastern Palace minister, the Emperor added Minister of Justice and made him prefect of Jiangning, removed his rhinoceros-horn belt, and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shixun had served in the crown prince's household, the emperor made him minister of justice and prefect of Jiangning, took back his rhinoceros-horn belt, and gave it to him as a parting gift.

sentences.zh: 後領定國軍節度使、知許州。

translations.literal: Later he also held the post of military commissioner of the Dingguo Army and prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later also served as military commissioner of the Dingguo Army and prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明道初，復入相，進中書侍郎兼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Mingdao era, he again entered the chancellorship and was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Mingdao era, he returned to the chancellorship as vice director of the Secretariat and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 明年，進門下侍郎、昭文館大學士、監修國史。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Academic Scholar of the Hall of Splendid Culture, and overseer of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made vice director of the Chancellery, grand academic scholar of the Hall of Splendid Culture, and overseer of the national history.

sentences.zh: 是歲旱蝗，士遜請如漢故事冊免，不許。

translations.literal: That year there was drought and locusts; Shixun requested, following Han precedent, to be removed by edict, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: That year drought and locusts struck. Shixun asked to be removed from office by edict, as in Han precedent, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 及帝自損尊號，士遜又請降官一等，以答天變，帝慰勉之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reduced his own honorific titles, Shixun again requested to be demoted one rank to answer Heaven's warning; the Emperor comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reduced his own honorific titles, Shixun again asked to be demoted one rank in response to Heaven's warning. The emperor comforted him and urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 群臣上章懿諡冊，退而入慰，士遜與同列過楊崇勳園飲，日中不至。

translations.literal: When the officials submitted the posthumous-title edict for Empress Yi and withdrew to enter and offer condolences, Shixun and his colleagues passed by Yang Chongxun's garden to drink and did not arrive until midday.
translations.idiomatic: After the officials presented the posthumous-title edict for Empress Yi and went in to offer condolences, Shixun and his colleagues stopped at Yang Chongxun's garden to drink and did not arrive until noon.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞范諷劾士遜，以尚書左僕射判河南府，崇勳亦以使相判許州。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Fan Feng impeached Shixun; he was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat with jurisdiction over Henan Prefecture, and Chongxun also became commissioner-governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Fan Feng impeached Shixun. Shixun was made left vice director of the Secretariat with jurisdiction over Henan Prefecture, and Chongxun was also sent out as commissioner-governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 翌日入謝，班崇勳下，帝問其故，士遜曰：「崇勳為使相，臣官僕射，位當下。」

translations.literal: The next day, when he entered to give thanks, he took his place below Chongxun. The Emperor asked why; Shixun said: "Chongxun is a commissioner-governor, while my office is vice director; my rank should be lower."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when he came to give thanks, he stood below Chongxun. The emperor asked why, and Shixun said, "Chongxun is a commissioner-governor, and I am only a vice director. My place should be lower."

sentences.zh: 遂為山南東道節度使、同中書門下平章事、判許州，以崇勳知陳州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he became military commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit, Co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and prefect of Xuzhou, while Chongxun was made prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made military commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit, co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and prefect of Xuzhou, while Chongxun was made prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時士遜罷已累日，制猶用宰相銜，有司但奉行制書，不復追改。

translations.literal: By then Shixun had already been dismissed for many days, yet the edict still used the chancellor's title; the offices simply carried out the edict and did not revise it.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shixun had been out of office for days, yet the edict still gave him a chancellor's title. The offices simply issued it as written and did not correct it.

sentences.zh: 徙河南府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寶元初，復以門下侍郎、兵部尚書入相，封郢國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoyuan era, he again entered the chancellorship as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Minister of War, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Baoyuan era, he returned to the chancellorship as vice director of the Chancellery and minister of war, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 士遜與輔臣奏事，帝從容曰：「朕昨放宮人，不獨閔幽閉，亦省浮費也。

translations.literal: When Shixun and the chief ministers reported on affairs, the Emperor said at ease: "Yesterday I released palace women—not only out of pity for those confined, but also to cut wasteful expense.
translations.idiomatic: While Shixun and the chief ministers were reporting on affairs, the emperor said casually, "Yesterday I released palace women—not only out of pity for those kept in seclusion, but also to cut unnecessary expense.

sentences.zh: 近復有獻孿女者，朕卻而弗受。」

translations.literal: Recently someone again presented twin girls, and I refused and did not accept them."
translations.idiomatic: Someone recently offered me twin girls as well, and I turned them away."

sentences.zh: 士遜曰：「此盛德事也。」

translations.literal: Shixun said: "This is a deed of great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Shixun said, "That is an act of great virtue."

sentences.zh: 帝徐曰：「近言者至有毀大臣、揭君過者。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said slowly: "Recently remonstrators have even gone so far as to slander great ministers and expose the ruler's faults."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said slowly, "Lately remonstrators have even slandered senior ministers and exposed the ruler's faults."

sentences.zh: 士遜曰：「陛下審察邪正，則憸訐之人，宜自戒懼矣。」

translations.literal: Shixun said: "If Your Majesty carefully distinguishes the wicked from the upright, then malicious slanderers should themselves be warned and afraid."
translations.idiomatic: Shixun said, "If Your Majesty carefully distinguishes wicked men from upright ones, malicious slanderers will themselves be warned into fear."

sentences.zh: 馮士元獄既具，帝以決獄問士遜。

translations.literal: After the Feng Shiyuan case was complete, the Emperor asked Shixun about deciding the trial.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Feng Shiyuan case was ready for judgment, the emperor asked Shixun how it should be decided.

sentences.zh: 士遜曰：「臺獄阿徇，非出自宸斷，何以愜中外之論邪。」

translations.literal: Shixun said: "The censorate prison fawns and bends; if the decision does not come from the imperial judgment, how can it satisfy opinion inside and outside the court?"
translations.idiomatic: Shixun said, "The censorate prison fawns and bends the law. Unless the decision comes from Your Majesty's own judgment, how can it satisfy opinion at court and beyond?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「君子小人各有黨乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Do gentlemen and petty men each have factions?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Do gentlemen and petty men each have factions of their own?"

sentences.zh: 士遜曰：「有之，第公私不同爾。」

translations.literal: Shixun said: "They do, only public and private are not the same."
translations.idiomatic: Shixun said, "They do, but the difference lies in public duty and private interest."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「法令必行，邪正有別，則朝綱舉矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If laws and orders are surely enforced and the wicked and upright are distinguished, then court discipline will be upheld."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If laws are enforced and the wicked are clearly separated from the upright, then court discipline will be restored."

sentences.zh: 康定初，士遜言禁兵久戍邊，其家在京師，有不能自存者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangding era, Shixun said that the imperial guard had long garrisoned the frontier, and that some of their families in the capital could not support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kangding era, Shixun reported that imperial guards had been garrisoned on the frontier for so long that some of their families in the capital could no longer support themselves.

sentences.zh: 帝命內侍條指揮使以下為差等，出內藏緡錢十萬賜之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered eunuchs to set grades below commanders and below, and disbursed one hundred thousand strings of cash from the inner treasury as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered eunuchs to rank the families of commanders and below by need, and gave out one hundred thousand strings of cash from the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 士遜又請遣使安撫陝西，帝命遣知制誥韓琦以行。

translations.literal: Shixun again requested sending an envoy to reassure Shaanxi; the Emperor ordered Drafting Academician Han Qi to go.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun also asked that an envoy be sent to reassure Shaanxi, and the emperor dispatched drafting academician Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 於是詔樞密院，自今邊事，並與士遜等參議。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to the Bureau of Military Affairs that from then on frontier affairs were all to be deliberated with Shixun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then instructed the Bureau of Military Affairs that from then on all frontier affairs were to be discussed with Shixun and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 及簡輦官為禁軍，輦官攜妻子遮宰相、樞密院喧訴，士遜方朝，馬驚墮地。

translations.literal: When palace carriage attendants were selected for the imperial guard, the attendants brought their wives and children to block the chancellor and the Bureau of Military Affairs in noisy appeal; Shixun was just then at court, and his horse was startled and he fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When palace carriage attendants were drafted into the imperial guard, they brought their wives and children to block the chancellor and the Bureau of Military Affairs in loud protest. Shixun was on his way to court when his horse bolted and threw him to the ground.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷多事，士遜亡所建明，諫官韓琦論曰：「政事府豈養病之地邪。」

translations.literal: At the time the court had many affairs, yet Shixun offered no proposals; remonstrance official Han Qi argued: "Is the Administration Hall a place for nursing illness?"
translations.idiomatic: The court was burdened with many crises, yet Shixun offered no constructive proposals. Remonstrance official Han Qi argued, "Is the Administration Hall a place for nursing one's health?"

sentences.zh: 士遜不自安，累上章請老，乃拜太傅，封鄧國公致仕。

translations.literal: Shixun felt ill at ease, repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement, and was then appointed Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Duke of Deng, and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in office, Shixun repeatedly memorialized to retire. He was made grand tutor, enfeoffed as Duke of Deng, and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔朔望朝見及大朝會，綴中書門下班，與一子五品服。

translations.literal: An edict granted him audience on the first and fifteenth of each month and at great court assemblies, to stand at the end of the Secretariat and Chancellery ranks, and granted one son fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed him to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month and at major assemblies, to stand at the end of the chancellery ranks, and granted one son fifth-rank robes.

sentences.zh: 士遜辭朝朔望。

translations.literal: Shixun declined the first- and fifteenth-day audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun declined the first- and fifteenth-day audiences.

sentences.zh: 間遣中使勞問，御書飛白「千歲」字賜之，士遜因建千歲堂。

translations.literal: From time to time the Emperor sent palace envoys to inquire after him and bestowed an imperial hand-written flying-white character reading "Thousand Years"; Shixun therefore built the Hall of Thousand Years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor occasionally sent palace envoys to inquire after him and gave him an imperial flying-white inscription reading "Thousand Years." Shixun built the Hall of Thousand Years in honor of the gift.

sentences.zh: 嘗請買城南官園，帝以賜士遜。

translations.literal: He once requested to buy the official garden south of the city, and the Emperor bestowed it on Shixun.
translations.idiomatic: He once asked to buy the official garden south of the city, and the emperor gave it to him outright.

sentences.zh: 宰相得謝，蓋自士遜始。

translations.literal: That a chancellor could retire with thanks began with Shixun.
translations.idiomatic: The formal retirement of a serving chancellor began with Shixun.

sentences.zh: 就第凡十年，卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: He remained at his residence for ten years in all, then died at age eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for ten years in all, then died at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝臨奠，贈太師、中書令，諡文懿，御篆其墓碑曰「舊德之碑」。

translations.literal: The Emperor came in person to offer sacrifice; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, given the posthumous name Wanyi, and the Emperor personally inscribed his tomb stele with the words "Stele of Former Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn him. Shixun was posthumously made grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat, given the posthumous name Wanyi, and the emperor personally inscribed his tomb stele with the words "Stele of Former Virtue."

sentences.zh: 士遜生七日，喪母，其姑育養之。

translations.literal: Seven days after Shixun was born, he lost his mother; his aunt raised and nurtured him.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun lost his mother when he was seven days old, and his aunt raised him.

sentences.zh: 既長，事姑孝謹，姑亡，為行服，徒跣扶柩以葬，追封南陽縣太君。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, he served his aunt with filial care and respect; when she died, he wore mourning garb, went barefoot, and supported the bier to the burial, and she was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Nanyang County.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he served his aunt with filial devotion. After she died, he wore mourning garb, went barefoot, and helped carry her coffin to burial. She was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Nanyang County.

sentences.zh: 初，陳堯佐罷參知政事，人有挾怨告堯佐謀反，復有誣諫官陰附宗室者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chen Yaozuo was dismissed as co-administrator of affairs, someone bearing a grudge reported that Yaozuo was plotting rebellion; there were also accusations that remonstrance officials secretly attached themselves to the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Chen Yaozuo was removed as co-administrator of affairs, a man with a grudge accused him of plotting rebellion, and others claimed that remonstrance officials were secretly aligned with members of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 士遜曰：「憸人構陷善良，以搖朝廷，奸偽一開，亦不能自保矣。」

translations.literal: Shixun said: "Malicious men frame the good to shake the court; once treachery and falsehood are opened, they too cannot preserve themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Shixun said, "Malicious men frame the innocent to shake the court. Once treachery and false accusation are allowed, even they cannot protect themselves."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，抵告者以罪，誣諫官事亦不下。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood, punished the accuser for the crime, and the matter of slandering remonstrance officials was also not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point, punished the accuser, and dropped the charges against the remonstrance officials as well.

sentences.zh: 然曹利用在樞府，藉寵肆威，士遜居其間，無所可否，時人以「和鼓」目之。

translations.literal: Yet Cao Liyong was in the Bureau of Military Affairs, relying on favor to wield power wantonly; Shixun sat among them and neither approved nor disapproved, and people of the time called him a "harmonizing drum."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cao Liyong held power in the Bureau of Military Affairs and abused imperial favor. Shixun sat among them and never clearly approved or opposed him, so contemporaries called him a "harmonizing drum."

sentences.zh: 士遜嘗納女口宮中，為御史楊偕所劾。

translations.literal: Shixun once presented women to the palace and was impeached by censor Yang Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun once presented women to the palace and was impeached by censor Yang Jie.

sentences.zh: 子友真，字益之。

translations.literal: His son Youzhen, styled Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youzhen, styled Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 初補將作監主簿，再遷為丞。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed chief clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and was later promoted to assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as chief clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and was later promoted to assistant director.

sentences.zh: 士遜為請館閣校勘，仁宗曰：「館閣所以待英俊，不可。」

translations.literal: Shixun requested for him the post of collator in the Hall of Literature; Emperor Renzong said: "The Hall of Literature is meant for outstanding talent; this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Shixun asked that he be made a collator in the Hall of Literature. Emperor Renzong said, "The Hall of Literature is reserved for outstanding talent. That will not do."

sentences.zh: 乃令館閣讀書，詔校勘毋得增員。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to study in the Hall of Literature, and an edict declared that collators were not to be added.
translations.idiomatic: He was instead allowed to study in the Hall of Literature, and an edict forbade adding new collator posts.

sentences.zh: 後編三館書籍，遷秘閣校理、同知禮院，賜進士出身，知襄州。

translations.literal: Later he compiled the books of the Three Halls, was promoted to collator in the Secret Archive and associate director of the Court of Rites, granted jinshi status, and made prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later helped compile the collections of the Three Halls, was promoted to collator in the Secret Archive and associate director of the Court of Rites, granted jinshi status, and made prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐軍賊張海剽劫不能制，罷歸。

translations.literal: Because bandit leader Zhang Hai plundered and he could not suppress him, he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and sent home after failing to suppress the bandit leader Zhang Hai.

sentences.zh: 後除史館修撰，御史何郯言：「史館修撰，故事，皆試知制誥，友直不當得。」

translations.literal: Later he was appointed compiler in the Historiography Office; censor He Tan said: "Compilers in the Historiography Office, by precedent, all had to pass the drafting-academician examination; Youzhi should not receive the post."
translations.idiomatic: He was later made compiler in the Historiography Office, but censor He Tan objected: "Historiography compilers were traditionally chosen only after passing the drafting-academician examination. Youzhi should not receive the post."

sentences.zh: 改集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: He was changed to compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies instead.

sentences.zh: 以天章閣待制知陝州，同勾當三班院。

translations.literal: As awaiting-draft academician of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns, he was made prefect of Shaanzhou and concurrently managed the Three-Rank Office.
translations.idiomatic: As awaiting-draft academician of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns, he served as prefect of Shaanzhou and concurrently managed the Three-Rank Office.

sentences.zh: 侍宴集英殿，猶衣緋衣，仁宗顧見之，乃賜金紫。

translations.literal: When he attended a banquet in the Hall of Spreading Excellence, he still wore scarlet robes; Emperor Renzong looked and saw this, and then bestowed gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the Hall of Spreading Excellence, he was still wearing scarlet robes. Emperor Renzong noticed and granted him gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部郎中、知越州。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Director in the Ministry of Works and prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Works and prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 州民每春斂財，大集僧道士女，謂之「祭天」，友直下令禁絕，取所斂財建學以延諸生。

translations.literal: Each spring the people of the prefecture collected money and gathered monks, Daoist priests, and women in great numbers, calling it "Sacrificing to Heaven"; Youzhi ordered it forbidden, took the collected money, and built a school to host students.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring the people of the prefecture collected money and gathered monks, Daoist priests, and women in a rite they called "Sacrificing to Heaven." Youzhi banned the practice, took the collected funds, and built a school for local students.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 士遜嘗記帝東宮舊事，而史官未之見，友直纂為《資善錄》上之。

translations.literal: Shixun had once recorded old affairs from the Emperor's Eastern Palace days, but the historiographers had not seen them; Youzhi compiled them into Records of Cultivating Goodness and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun had recorded old stories from the emperor's days in the Eastern Palace that the historiographers had never seen. Youzhi compiled them into Records of Cultivating Goodness and submitted the work.

sentences.zh: 幼子友正，字義祖，杜門不治家事，居小閣學書，積三十年不輟，遂以書名。

translations.literal: His youngest son Youzheng, styled Yizu, shut his doors and did not manage household affairs; he lived in a small loft studying calligraphy, accumulating thirty years without stopping, and thus became famous for his writing.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Youzheng, styled Yizu, shut himself away from household affairs and spent thirty unbroken years in a small loft practicing calligraphy until he became renowned for his writing.

sentences.zh: 神宗評其草書，為本朝第一。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong judged his cursive script the first of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong judged his cursive script the finest of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 論曰：呂夷簡、張士遜皆以儒學起家，列位輔弼。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Lü Yijian and Zhang Shixun both rose from Confucian learning and took places as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Lü Yijian and Zhang Shixun both rose through Confucian learning to serve as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 仁宗之世，天下承平，因時制宜，濟以寬厚，相臣預有力焉。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Renzong, the realm enjoyed peace; adapting measures to the times and tempering them with leniency, the chief ministers had a share in the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Renzong's reign the realm enjoyed peace. The chief ministers helped shape policy to fit the times and tempered it with leniency.

sentences.zh: 士遜練習民事，風跡可紀，而依違曹利用以取譏。

translations.literal: Shixun was practiced in civilian affairs and his conduct was worth recording, yet by wavering with Cao Liyong he drew reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun was experienced in civilian affairs and left a record worth noting, but by wavering with Cao Liyong he drew criticism.

sentences.zh: 方夷簡在下僚，諸父蒙正以宰相才期之。

translations.literal: When Yijian was still in lower office, his uncle Mengzheng expected in him the talent of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yijian was still a junior official, his uncle Mengzheng already expected in him the talent of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及其為相，深謀遠慮，有古大臣之度焉。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, his deep planning and far-sighted concern had the measure of the great ministers of old.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became chancellor, his deep planning and far-sighted judgment showed the measure of the great ministers of old.

sentences.zh: 在位日久，頗務收恩避怨，以固權利，郭后之廢，遂成其君之過舉，咎莫大焉。

translations.literal: He held office for a long time and greatly sought to gather favor and avoid resentment to secure power and profit; the deposition of Empress Guo thus became his lord's grave error, and the blame for it was immense.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for many years and worked hard to gather favor and avoid resentment in order to secure his power. The deposition of Empress Guo became his sovereign's gravest mistake, for which the blame was immense.

sentences.zh: 雖然，呂氏更執國政，三世四人，世家之盛，則未之有也。

translations.literal: Even so, the Lü clan held state power in succession—four men across three generations—and the splendor of such a great house had never been seen before.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, the Lü clan held state power in succession—four men across three generations—a level of family eminence unmatched in the dynasty.
